# BIM door: how an AI drives UNION

# The guide
UNION is a complete building-modelling and drafting program: walls, floors, roofs and stairs; freeform (NURBS) curves and surfaces; structure and building services; blocks; materials with photographic textures and a node graph; views, schedules, sheets and printing; realistic pictures. An AI works in UNION through the calls in this guide. UNION AI, the AI built into UNION, works this way for the drafter, and AI labs and researchers reach the same calls through UNION's MCP door on a free research licence.

THIS GUIDE. It is written for AI agents. It is the guide that ships inside UNION 1.0.0-beta.2, cut down to what has been played through UNION's AI door: calls not yet played, and the notes on them, are left out. The guide inside UNION holds the rest and is read by part with `get_guide`; the part numbers here are the same as there, so a number missing here is a part kept in the program.

THE RULE. This guide is not the extent of UNION. UNION can do nearly every operation you already know from building-modelling, drafting and 3D programs. Your job is to look the control up, never to decide it is absent. Part 2 says where UNION lists its commands, dialogs, ops and cards. Before you tell the person that UNION lacks a thing, you must have:
1. looked for the everyday word in part 3 (the map) and the name in part 16 (every command);
2. asked UNION itself: `commands_list {"name":"<name>"}` or `commands_list {"tab":"<tab>"}`, and `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > <name>"}`;
3. tried it and read UNION's answer: a refusal names its fix and often lists the valid words.
Still not found? Say "I did not find a control for <thing>; I searched <the lists>". Never say "UNION cannot".

HOW TO WORK. Act at once and decide. Ask the person only what neither the model, a look-up nor a sensible choice of yours settles, and say what you chose. Read the model first: `document_info {"categories":true}`, `levels_list`, `views_list`. Write with `ops_run` where an op line exists (part 4), else with `commands_run` or a step (part 5). Look at a picture after each batch of writes (part 6). Read UNION's words in every answer, not only "ok" or "green". File actions (such as New, Open, Save As, Close, Import, Export, Print) are the person's own presses: ask for one in a single short sentence.

READ BY PART. Name a part by the start of its heading, number and dot included: `get_guide {"part":"guide > 4. Fast ops"}`. A part of up to 24 KB answers whole; a longer one answers its opening text and a list of its pieces. Read one piece of any part by a word of its heading: `get_guide {"part":"gable"}` answers the first heading that holds the word and names the others. Words match headings only, never the text: no match means only that no heading holds the word. Read part 2 once, then only what the job needs. The reference (every command, dialog, field and parameter of UNION) is a separate document: `get_guide {"part":"reference"}`.

STANDING. The calls on this page are the ones marked played in UNION's own guide: each was run through UNION's AI door on a UNION build. A played call is true of its build only: send the call and read UNION's answer.

TWO TOWERS. The last part of this page is a worked set of 15 prompts that draws two steel towers, a gridshell round them and a drawing set of 24 sheets, call by call: read `Two Towers > Rules`, then `Two Towers > Prompt <n>`.

## 1. Connect, permissions, and working beside other agents
Look commands, dialogs and fields up and drive them with `commands_list`, `commands_run` and `steps_run`: part 2.

In this part:
- The tools, one line each, by group.
- What is the person's, not yours: File actions (Save excepted), the working copy, `start:` lines, Undo.
- Busy, unavailable and retry answers.

Look it up: the model's facts and the reference's parts:

    document_info {"categories":true}
    get_guide {"part":"reference"}

### The union tools at a glance

Arguments are the tool descriptions. A reply is read in the reference under the tool's method, its name with the first underscore a dot (`record_start` is `record.start`, `albatross_card_readback` is `albatross.card_readback`; the second for `wall_profile_get` and `line_weights_model`): `get_guide {"part":"reference > Methods"}`. The needs column: R = a read; W = a write. Units are mm. A paged tool takes `after` and answers `more` and `next`.

| tool and arguments | what it does | needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Read the model** | | |
| `document_info {categories?}` | path, name, revision, counts; `categories` adds a count per category | R |
| `elements_query {category, level?, type?, fields?, limit?, after?}` | a page of elements; the category in any spelling the catalogue knows | R |
| `element_get {id}` | one element: columns, parameters, `host`, `location` | R |
| `elements_get {ids}` | up to 200 elements as `element_get`; ids that are no element in `missing` | R |
| `params_schema {category?}` | the parameter rows of a category; none lists the categories | R |
| `types_list {category, limit?, after?}` | the project's types of a category, with layers | R |
| `levels_list {}` | levels by elevation | R |
| `grids_list {limit?, after?}` | grids: id, Name, geometry | R |
| `groups_list {limit?, after?, instances?}` | group definitions with member and instance counts | R |
| `views_list {kind?}` | views: id, name, kind | R |
| `sheets_list {limit?, after?}` | sheets by number with the views placed on each | R |
| `schedule_read {view, limit?, after?}` | a schedule's table as the schedule shows it | R |
| `library_list {category, limit?, after?}` | block names of a category (a category is needed); on a build that lists them, Detail Items and Generic Annotations add the detail components as `Family : Type`; reads no document | R |
| `model_check {limit?, after?}` | the structural analytical model check | R |
| `selection_get {}` | the selection | R |
| `elements_in_box {view?, points}` | ids inside a view's box and those it touches; selects nothing | R |
| `detail_shape {id, kind?}` | the drawing of a detail component, line or tag, in mm | R |
| `redline_marks {}` | the mark-ups beside the open model | R |
| **Write the model** | | |
| `param_set {ids, key, value}` | one parameter on up to 5000 elements, all or none | W |
| `type_duplicate {category, type, family?, name}` | a type copied with its parameters and layers | W |
| `type_set {category, type, family?, key, value}` | one parameter of a type; elements on it follow | W |
| `selection_set {ids}` | replaces the selection; `[]` clears it | W |
| `redline_answer {id, status, words}` | answers one mark-up: Done, Query or Refused | W |
| **Look** | | |
| `view_image {view?, window?, width?}` | a PNG of a UNION window; `window` is main, viewer, active, or a program's window by name; width 64 to 2048; a 3D view in front is waited on up to 20 seconds | R |
| `view_activate {view}` | shows a view or sheet by name or id; a name two views share is refused: send the id from `views_list` | R |
| `view_camera {view?, azimuth?, pitch?, fit?, ids?}` | turns and frames a 3D view, reads its camera | R |
| **Run commands and steps** | | |
| `commands_list {tab?, kind?, built?, name?, brief?}` | the command registry; no argument gives the tabs with counts | R |
| `commands_run {name, options?, points?, finish?}` | one command as its ribbon press; at most 40 points a call | W |
| `ops_run {lines, name?}` | 1 to 500 op lines, one Undo entry `Add-in: <name>` | W |
| `steps_run {steps}` | 1 to 200 step lines, one undo step; a red step ends the call | W |
| `batch {calls}` | up to 100 `param.set`, `selection.set`, `commands.run` calls, one undo step | W |
| **ALBATROSS** | | |
| `albatross_place {kind, at?, inputs?}` | places a card; opens the ALBATROSS window if closed | W |
| `albatross_set {card, input, value}` | sets one input or setting of a card | W |
| `albatross_wire {from, output?, to, input}` | wires an output into an input | W |
| `albatross_delete {card}` | deletes a card and its wires; elements it made stay; opens the ALBATROSS window if closed | W |
| `albatross_graph {limit?, after?}` | the cards and wires; opens the ALBATROSS window if closed | R |
| `albatross_card_readback {card, part, offset?, snapshot?}` | one card's Panel text or ports; a closed canvas answers unavailable | R |
| **Talk with the person** | | |
| `falcon_wait {timeout_ms?}` | takes the person's next prompt; `{none:true}` at the time-out | R |
| `falcon_say {text, done?}` | shows your words in their conversation; `done` ends your answer | R |
| **The guide** | | |
| `get_guide {part?, page?}` | this guide, and the reference by `reference > <section> > <name>`, for example `reference > Commands > Freeform Curve` | R |

### What is the person's, not yours: File actions

File actions are the person's: New, Open, Import, Export; also Save As, Close, Exit, Print and every Export or Import format. Save is the one File action you may press (below).
UNION's own words end the matter, except `busy`: do not retry, tell the person which control to press. Nothing was saved, opened, written or ended.
- A File control, by a step or by `commands_run`: "cannot proceed: 'Save As' is the person's own control, not UNION AI's; ask the person to press it". The word between the quotes is the control. A `batch` holding one stops there.
- A command that is a dialog: "cannot proceed: Print needs a person". Export and Import read the same with their name.
- Save: UNION AI's Save keeps unsaved edits in its own copy, never in the person's file. The copy is `<model> - <UNION AI's name><the model's own suffix>` in UNION AI's folder, `<UNION state folder>/<UNION AI's name>`; a UNION 2D drawing makes a `.u2d` copy. Making that copy leaves the person's file and backups, saved mark, Undo, star and Recent as they were. The status bar says `<UNION AI's name> saved its copy of <model>. Your file is unchanged until you press Save.`; when replacing its earlier copy, it says `<UNION AI's name> replaced '<copy name>'. Your file is unchanged until you press Save.` If a copy already made at the same journal state is still in that folder, Save writes nothing again. If the model has a person's file and nothing unsaved, Save writes nothing.
- Undo and Redo act on the entries your calls made, each named `Add-in: <name>`; as steps: part 5. When the newest change is the person's: "cannot proceed: the newest change is the person's own, not UNION AI's; ask the person to undo it". Nothing is undone.

Unsaved edits live in the working copy; the person's own Save keeps them in the person's file. UNION AI's Save keeps unsaved edits in its own copy, never in the person's file. The copy is `<model> - <UNION AI's name><the model's own suffix>` in UNION AI's folder, `<UNION state folder>/<UNION AI's name>`; a UNION 2D drawing makes a `.u2d` copy. Making that copy leaves the person's file and backups, saved mark, Undo, star and Recent as they were. The status bar says `<UNION AI's name> saved its copy of <model>. Your file is unchanged until you press Save.`; when replacing its earlier copy, it says `<UNION AI's name> replaced '<copy name>'. Your file is unchanged until you press Save.` If a copy already made at the same journal state is still in that folder, Save writes nothing again. The door's answers stay the same as above.

`start:` lines. The recipes of this guide that were played on a fresh template copy begin with a step like this:

    start:Architectural · picks — · keys — · fields — · expect view Ground active

On the person's door the model is the one they have open. Leave every `start:` line out; it is red: "cannot proceed: 'New' is the person's own control, not UNION AI's; ask the person to press it". A red step ends the call, so a recipe that begins with one plays nothing. Read the model instead: `document_info {"categories":true}`, `views_list {}`, `levels_list {}`, and use the names it holds in the recipe's `expect` words (the Structural template opens on Level 1, not Ground).

### Busy, unavailable and retry answers

Retry these. Send the same call again after a short wait.
- One drawing call at a time across callers. A second caller is answered "another AI chat's drawing call is still running in UNION; retry in a moment".
- `busy` from `view_activate`, `view_image` or `view_camera`: the person has a tool or dialog open, or UNION is working or opening a model.
- "cannot proceed: the 3D view is still building its model; ask for the picture again in a moment" (`view_image`, no picture). If it answers so again and again while UNION is idle, the main window is minimised or behind the UNION AI window. Send `view_image {"window":"main"}` with NO `view` named: it returns the picture as it stands.
- `unavailable` "cannot proceed: the Albatross window did not open" (any `albatross_` tool): ask the person to open ALBATROSS, then send the call again.

Do not retry: the answers of the piece on what is the person's (File actions, the person's newest change), except `busy`, which is asked again in a moment. A wrong word is not a retry: UNION's refusal names the fix and lists the valid words: part 13 (UNION's words).

## 2. Find any control: look it up before you say it is missing
In this part: where UNION states its counts; the calls that list its commands, dialogs, fields, parameters, types and blocks; the calls that read the open model; the three routes from a name to a run; how to report a gap.

THE RULE: this guide is not the extent of UNION. UNION does nearly every operation you already know. Your job is to look the control up. A control the guide does not show is one you have not found yet. Say "not found in <the lists searched>" and nothing stronger.

Look it up, in this order:
1. Part 16 (Index): the command names by tab and panel, one read.
2. Part 3 (The map): everyday words mapped to UNION's names.
3. `commands_list` with a `tab` or an exact `name`: the command in full. A keyword goes to items 1 and 2.
4. `get_guide` with `reference`: every command, dialog, field, op kind and parameter, exact.
5. `params_schema`, `types_list`, `library_list`: parameter rows, types, blocks.
6. A wrong word on purpose: UNION's refusal lists the valid words.

Look it up: `get_guide {"part":"reference"}`, `commands_list {}`, `params_schema {}`.

### How much UNION holds: where each count stands

| What | Where to read it | What it counts |
|---|---|---|
| Commands by name | `commands_list {}` answers `count`; a call with `tab`, `kind`, `built` or `name` answers `count` for its rows | What `commands_list` answers and `commands_run` takes. `built` false marks a command with no handler. |
| Commands on a tab | `commands_list {}`: `tabs` as `[{tab, count}]`, and `no_tab` | The commands of each tab. The commands that name no tab are menu entries, viewer, wind, layer, program tiles, dialog openers and the `file-import:` and `file-export:` names. |
| Dialogs | the heading `Dialogs (N)` of `get_guide {"part":"reference > Dialogs"}` | The reference part "Dialogs". The program builds further dialogs in code; they are not among them. |
| Parameter rows | `params_schema {}` answers `count` of the categories and each category's `rows`; the heading `Parameters (N categories)` of the reference | The rows of every category. A category answered with `open: true` stores more than its rows list. |
| Op kinds | the heading `Ops grammar (N kinds)` of the reference | Fast-op line shapes (part 4). |
| Blocks | `library_list {"category":"<category>"}` answers `total` | The blocks of the shipped library (part 8). |

- The reference heading `Commands (N)` counts one entry for each key, not one for each command: it differs from the `count` of `commands_list`. They are views of one list: never add them.
- A count is what was listed, never a limit.

### Look-up calls for UNION's own words: get_guide and the reference

`get_guide`: the guide and the reference.

    get_guide {}
The opening, then one line per `##` heading with its size.

Two ways to name a part of the guide. A bare word finds the first heading that holds it anywhere and names the others: `get_guide {"part":"gable"}`. A path names a part by the START of each heading, number and dot first, and each step is searched inside the one before. A word from the middle of a heading does not match in a path: `guide > 4 > schedule` answered `No part of the guide has ... in its heading`; `guide > 3 > Walls, floors` and `guide > 4 > Roofs, stairs` found their pieces. Words match headings only, never the text. If a path finds nothing, send the bare word. A part of up to 24 KB answers whole; a longer part with pieces answers its opening text and a sized list of its pieces. A piece of any part is read alone by a word of its heading.

No match answers `No part of the guide has "<words>" in its heading. Call get_guide with no part for the guide's contents; the reference is a separate document: part "reference".`. UNION's own words may differ slightly.

    get_guide {"part":"reference"}
Six parts with sizes: Writing a C++ add-in (1.7 KB), Methods (24.4 KB), Commands (357.2 KB), Dialogs (157.8 KB), Ops grammar (6.5 KB), Parameters (59.6 KB).

    get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > Freeform Curve"}
One command in full.

A command's heading is its `name` as `commands_list` prints it; a few commands are filed under another word. When `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > <name>"}` finds no heading, `commands_list {"name":"<name>"}` gives the same facts. `reference > Commands > draw-stair-settings` and `reference > Commands > form-panels-dialog` found no heading. Else try the ribbon word: part 16 (Index) gives the tab and panel.

    get_guide {"part":"reference > Dialogs > Display Options"}
One dialog: Title, Buttons (OK, Cancel, Apply), Actions (Save as View Template), then a table Tab, Group, Field, Key, Kind, Limits, Choices, Notes, with the fields Style, Show Edges, Transparency (0-100), Silhouette Edges, Silhouette Line Style, Shadows and more. A dialog heading begins with the word Dialog, so write the address `reference > Dialogs > Dialog <name>`; `Display Options` worked because no earlier dialog heading holds those words. A dialog's Title line is what UNION prints. `Category Styles` prints `Object Styles`.

### Look-up calls for commands: commands_list

    commands_list {}
`count` 1020, `no_tab` 483, `tabs` as `[{tab, count}]`, and a `more` line on how to ask next.

    commands_list {"brief":true,"tab":"View"}
Short rows: `name`, the other name, `tab`, `panel`, `kind`, `built`. `kind` is `tool`, `action` or `dialog`. Without `brief`, `tab` answers that tab's commands in full.

    commands_list {"name":"Freeform Curve"}
Every command of that exact name. Each row: `name`, the other name, `tab`, `panel`, `kind`, `built`, `key`, `prompt`, `draw_modes`, `options`; each option `{name, label, kind, default, choices, scope, modes?}`. Send an option's `name`, not its `label` (`Level` is labelled Storey). An option with `modes` is offered in those draw modes; one without is offered in every mode.

- Two commands may share a name. `Loft` answers two rows: tab Structural panel Form (curves), and tab Make panel Forms (profiles with a Void option). `commands_run` by that name ran the Freeform one each time.
- A command's tab is the registry's tab, not always the ribbon's. Freeform Curve, Loft, Sweep and Revolve sit on tab Structural, panel Form.
- `name` takes UNION's own name of a command, and some common trade names too: `commands_list {"name":"Level","brief":true}` answered the command `Storey`; `Shaft` answered `Vertical Cut-out`; `Ref Plane` answered `Construction Plane`; `Dormer` answered `Roof Cut-out`. It matches names, not the words of prompts: `Gable`, `Skylight`, `Curtain Wall`, `NURBS` and `Spline` answered `count: 0`. A word that finds nothing is not a missing feature: the gable roof is recipe (s) of part 14 (Recipes); a curtain wall is a wall of a type whose Function is Curtain (part 4, Fast ops); look in part 3 (The map) and part 16 (Index).
- Words found under UNION's names: NURBS work is `Freeform Curve`, `Loft`, `Sweep`, `Revolve`; a spline line is a Model Line (the command list's `3D Line`) with `Draw=Spline`.

### Look-up calls for parameters, types and blocks: params_schema, types_list, library_list, and a wrong word on purpose

`params_schema`, `types_list`, `library_list`: the words of a category.

    params_schema {}
The 29 categories with their row counts.

    params_schema {"category":"Doors"}
`{category, count, rows, open}`. `open: true` means an element stores more than the rows list; `param_set` sets a further parameter by name. A row that begins with `@` is an element column. `param_set` writes `@type` (the element's type) where its row is not `readOnly`, and a floor's `@level` (a level name). It refuses a row marked `readOnly`: `cannot proceed: '<row>' is read-only and cannot be set; nothing was written`. A name the catalogue does not know answers `not_found`.

    param_set {"ids":["<wall id>"],"key":"@type","value":"Block 190 Core-filled"}
Answered `{"changed":1,"elements":1}`; `element_get` then read the new family and type. The same call on a roof, with a roof type name from `types_list`, answered the same. `op:set id=<id> key=Type value=...` answered `A Roof has no parameter 'Type'`.

    types_list {"category":"Floors"}
`{category, total, count, types:[{id, family, name, layers?}], more, next?}`. `layers` give function, material and thickness in mm.

    library_list {"category":"Furniture","limit":5}
The Block Database's block names of a category, no model read. It answered `{"category":"Furniture","count":5,"more":true,"names":["Armchair","Banquette Booth","Bar Stool","Bed - Bunk","Bed - Double"],"next":5,"total":204}`. `limit` pages it; `next` is the place to go on from. `library_list {}` answers `library.list needs a category`.

A wrong word on purpose: UNION answers with the valid words.

    view_activate {"view":"Ground"}
`cannot proceed: 2 views answer to 'Ground': Ground (Floor Plan, id 48660e38...) and Ground (Ceiling Plan, id 5cde2487...); name the one wanted by its id; ...`.

Other answers of this kind:
- `op:add material library=zinc_standing_seam ...` answered `cannot proceed: the library holds no texture set named 'zinc_standing_seam'; nothing was written`.
- A wrong row, item or option in a step's `fields` lists the valid ones. `table 'Patterns' has no row 'zzz' (its rows: Solid fill, Diagonal crosshatch, ...)` lists a dialog table's rows. `the options strip has no 'Offset' (its options: Storey (Level), Width, Height, Diameter, ...)` lists the strip's options.
- A wrong op kind lists the kinds. The call:

      op:add gable at=(0,0)
  UNION's words: `cannot proceed: 'gable' is not a kind of add (add column, add grid, add level, add beam, add brace, add wall, add floor, add roof, add ceiling, add material, add room, add shaft, add stair, ...)` and goes on through every kind (the list is in part 4, Fast ops).
- A wrong material key lists the 33 keys a material keeps. The call:

      op:set material name="Play White" key=zzz value=1
  UNION's words: `cannot proceed: a material keeps no 'zzz' (its keys: density, elastic_modulus, poisson_ratio, yield_strength, rigidity_modulus, tensile_strength, compressive_strength, thermal_expansion, heat_conductivity, render_colour, texture, texture_size, texture_rotation, roughness, metallic, bump, transparency, glow, relief_depth, relief_shadow, height_gain, cut_pattern, surface_pattern, shading_colour, surface_pattern_angle, surface_pattern_follows, description, material_class, material_keynote, material_mark, material_comments, manufacturer, cost)`. Which keys change the Realistic view: part 7 (Materials).
- A wrong card kind lists every kind: `albatross_place {"kind":"zzz"}` answers `cannot proceed: the Albatross library has no card kind 'zzz'. Kinds by group: Model: Beam, Brace, Column ...` and goes on through every group (part 10, ALBATROSS).

### Look-up calls that read what is drawn

    document_info {"categories":true}
Path, name, revision and counts (of the working copy), and a count for each category present, annotation categories too (Dimensions, Text Notes, Lines, Tags, Keynotes). `elements_query` takes the category names it prints.

    levels_list {}
Levels by elevation. A level's id is `level-<name>`.

    views_list {"kind":"Floor Plan"}
`id`, `name`, `kind` of each view; give `kind` to narrow it. When two views share a name, name the view by its id: `view_activate` refuses a shared name, and an op's `view=` takes the floor plan where a floor plan and a ceiling plan share it.

    elements_query {"category":"Freeform Curve"}
Elements of a category, keyset page. Rows come under `rows`. The category is read under any spelling the catalogue knows; a name that is no category answers `not_found`. `level` and `type` narrow the rows; `fields` chooses the columns. It answers 100 rows unless `limit` is given.

    element_get {"id":"<curve id>"}
One element: its columns, decoded `params` (`"Control Points":5,"Degree":3,"Interpolate":true`), `host` and `location` in mm. A view's id answers the view's rows: `element_get {"id":"view-3d"}`.

### From a name to running it: the three routes

Read the row of the name first (`commands_list {"name":"<name>"}` or the reference), then take the route its row points to.

ROUTE 1: an op line (part 4). Use it when `reference > Ops grammar` has a kind for the work. Two lines of a played batch:

    ops_run {"name":"Walls and floor","lines":["op:add wall from=(0,0) to=(8000,0) level=Ground","op:add floor boundary=(0,0),(8000,0),(8000,6000),(0,6000) level=Ground"]}
Each result holds the new element's id in `made`.

ROUTE 2: `commands_run` with options and points (part 5). Use it for a tool or action command with options and points. Shape: `{name, options?, points?, finish?}`. `options` take the option `name`s of the row; `points` are model x, y in mm; `finish` true presses Finish after the points. Its reply is `commands.run` in the reference.

    commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"3","Interpolate":true},"points":[[0,0],[3000,1500],[6000,-1000],[9000,800],[12000,0]],"finish":true}
Answer: `{"changed":[{"category":"Freeform Curve","id":"deea7bc2...","kind":"insert","table":"element"}],"text":"Freeform Curve: 5 point(s)"}`.

A command that wants a selection first: select, then run. Points do not pick elements.

    selection_set {"ids":["<curve 1>","<curve 2>","<curve 3>"]}
    commands_run {"name":"Loft"}
One `Form` element, a surface through the curves in the order selected. With nothing selected UNION answers `cannot proceed: Select the Freeform Curves to loft through, in order, then press Enter`.

- Played the same way: `Revolve` (select the profile curve; the `points` are the axis start and end, and with none UNION answered `Revolve: 0 point(s)`), `Sweep` (select the rail, then the section) and `Clip Box` (a cutaway box).
- After a command, read back `document_info {"categories":true}` and do not send the call twice.
- A tool left standing swallows the next call's points. Clear it: `steps_run {"steps":["chrome:Canvas Zoom to Fit · picks — · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect —"]}`.
- A tool's draw mode (arc, spline, Pick Walls ...: its `draw_modes`) is set with `fields Options Strip: Draw=<mode>` in the tool's ribbon step, never in `commands_run` options (part 5, Commands, steps and dialogs). Played: Roof with `Draw=Pick Walls`, Wall with `Draw=Start-End-Radius Arc`, Model Line (the command list's `3D Line`) with `Draw=Spline`.

ROUTE 3: a ribbon step with fields (part 5). Use it when the work is a dialog's fields. The chain: the reference row of the command gives `Step:` and `Opens:`; the dialog's table gives the field labels and their choices.

    steps_run {"steps":["ribbon:View:Display Options · picks — · keys — · fields Display Options: Style=Realistic; Show Edges=no; Silhouette Edges=no; Shadows=yes; Soft Shadows=yes; Backdrop=Sky; OK= · expect —"]}
Every field read back and UNION said `'OK' pressed; the dialog closed`.

- A step is five parts: `<driver>:<control path> · picks <points or —> · keys <keys or —> · fields <Dialog: Field=value; … or —> · expect <words>`. The middle dot separates parts, the em dash is an empty part, the arrow `›` folds a sub-tool: `ribbon:Manage:Additional Settings › Fill Patterns`.
- Name the dialog in `fields` by the title UNION prints, the Title line of the reference.
- End a dialog's fields with `OK=`.
- A `Step:` that starts `contextual:` presses a button of a contextual tab, which stands while its selection or sketch does: `contextual:Finish`.

### Report a gap honestly: what you looked in, what UNION said, two honest forms

Before you write "not found", have done all of these:
1. Part 16 (Index): read the tab groups and the "(no tab)" group for the name and its neighbours.
2. Part 3 (The map): try the everyday word and its neighbours.
3. `commands_list` by exact `name` (singular and plural) and by `tab`.
4. The reference: Commands, Dialogs (a field you want may sit in a dialog), Parameters (a parameter row), Ops grammar.
5. `params_schema`, `types_list`, `library_list` (the work may be a type, a parameter or a block, not a command).
6. A wrong word on purpose, and read UNION's words.

A thing is often found under another word. A command sits on a tab that is not the ribbon's (Freeform Curve is on tab Structural). A dialog's name differs from its title (`Category Styles` prints `Object Styles`).

Two honest forms; use no other:
- UNION's own refusal, quoted exactly.
- "not found in <the lists searched>".

Never turn a failed search into a limit.

Say four things: the lists you searched, the call you tried, UNION's words in quotes, and what you did instead with the next press. A model sentence:

- A refusal: "UNION answered 'cannot proceed: Select the Freeform Curves to loft through, in order, then press Enter'; I selected the three curves and ran Loft again."

Look it up: `get_guide {"part":"reference"}`, `commands_list {}`, `params_schema {}`, `document_info {"categories":true}`, part 16 (Index).

## 3. The map: what UNION can make and do, from the word you know to UNION's name
In this part: fifteen pieces, one per kind of work. Each line gives the everyday words, UNION's own name for the thing, and the shortest route to it. Read the piece for the work in hand by a word of its heading: `get_guide {"part":"roofs"}`, `get_guide {"part":"NURBS"}`, `get_guide {"part":"schedules"}`.

How to use a line:
1. Take UNION's name from it.
2. Read that command in full, with its prompt, options and draw modes: `commands_list {"name":"<name>"}`.
3. Run it: an op line (part 4), or `commands_run` or a step (part 5).

A word that is in no piece is not a missing feature. Look for it among the command names of part 16, then ask UNION (part 2). This map is long and still not the whole of UNION.

Look it up: `commands_list {}` gives the tabs and their counts; `commands_list {"name":"Level","brief":true}` shows a trade name finding UNION's own (`Storey`).

### Site, levels, grids and setting out (terrain, topo, contours, property line, survey point, true north, storey, landscape, parking, datum)
Levels, plan views, grids, reference planes, terrain, site boundary, location, site imports. Tabs: Setout, Freeform (Site), Views, Manage, Detailing, Insert.

- level, storey, floor level, datum, elevation, RL: `op:add level`, tool `Storey`. Route: ops_run `op:add level elevation=3000 name="Level 2"`; move or rename `op:set id="level-Level 1" key=Elevation value=3600` (id keeps the old name). `commands_list {"name":"Level","brief":true}` answers `Storey`.
- plan view, floor plan, structural plan, reflected ceiling plan, RCP: `op:add view`, `Plans`. Route: ops_run `op:add view kind=plan level="Level 2"` (kind plan, structural, ceiling); step `ribbon:View:Plan Views › Floor Plan · picks — · keys Return · fields New Plan: Levels=Level 2 · expect dialog closed`. Two views share a name (Ground): `view_activate` refuses the name (`cannot proceed: 2 views answer to 'Ground'`) and an op's `view=` takes the floor plan; name the view by its id from views_list, `view=<id>`. North arrow: `op:add symbol at=(-9000,30000) view=<plan id>`.
- typical floor, repeat storey, stack floors, copy up: `op:array`, `Paste › Aligned to Selected Levels`. Route: ops_run `op:array id=<ids> count=12 step=(0,0,3600)`.
- grid, gridline, axis, column grid: `op:add grid`, tool `Gridline`. Route: ops_run `op:add grid from=(0,-2000) to=(0,12000) name=A`.
- curved grid, arc grid, radial grid, grid from lines: `Gridline` modes Line, Start-End-Radius Arc, Center-ends Arc, Pick Lines, Multi-Segment. `Draw=` in the tool's own ribbon step was played on Roof, Wall and Model Line.
- scope box, reference plane, construction plane, work plane: `Extent Box` (Name, Height 3000), `Construction Plane` (Offset), `Set Plane`, `Show Plane`, `Plane View`, dialog `Work Plane`. `commands_list {"name":"Ref Plane"}` answered `Construction Plane`.
- location, latitude, longitude, true north, shared coordinates, base point, georeference: dialog `Location`, `Rotate Project North`, `Rotate True North`, `Mirror Project`, `Specify Coordinates at a Point`, `Acquire Coordinates`, `Publish Coordinates`, `Report Shared Coordinates`, `Relocate Project`, `Place Project Base Point`, `ifc-georef`. `OK=` was played on Display Options.
- roads, footpaths, lawns, verges, driveways: floors on site levels. Route: ops_run `op:add level elevation=<mm> name=<name>`, then `op:add floor boundary=(0,0) (8000,0) (8000,6000) (0,6000) level=<name>`. Name the lowest site level like "Ground": the landscape pad stands there, lower parts are buried.
- trees, shrubs, people, cars, benches, street lights, retaining walls: block categories Planting, Entourage, Parking, Furniture, Lighting Fixtures, Geotechnical, Structural Foundations. Route: library_list {"category":"Planting"}, then `op:place block family=<name> type=<type> at=(x,y) level=<name>`.

Look it up: commands_list {"tab":"Freeform"}, {"tab":"Manage"}, {"name":"Gridline"}; get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > Toposurface"}; params_schema {"category":"Levels"} (also Grids, Toposolid). Steps: part 5.

### Walls, floors, ceilings, stairs, ramps, railings and rooms (curved wall, arc wall, slab, spiral stair, area, shaft)

- wall, partition: `op:add wall`, `Wall: Architectural`, `Wall: Structural`. Route: ops_run `op:add wall from=(0,0) to=(8000,0) level=Ground`; by picks: `ribbon:Structure:Wall` (`Wall`) and `ribbon:Architecture:Wall` (`Wall: Architectural`), both green.
- wall height, top, base offset, location line: rows Unconnected Height, Base Offset, Top Offset, Location Line. Route: `op:set id=<wall> key="Unconnected Height" value=3120`; set Base Offset after the height. `height=` on `op:add wall` is the wall's own height from its level: with `level="Level 1" height=2700` the wall stands at z = 3000.
- curved wall, arc wall, circular wall, polygon wall: `steps_run {"steps":["ribbon:Architecture:Wall · picks (50000,6000) (56000,6000) (53000,8000) · keys Escape Escape · fields Options Strip: Draw=Start-End-Radius Arc · expect Walls +1"]}` (start, end, a point on the arc).
- wall type, layers, wall colour: types_list {"category":"Walls"}; `type_set {"category":"Walls","type":"Generic 200mm","key":"Layer 1 Material","value":"Play White"}` answers the layers. Set every layer: Realistic draws the structure layer. Change a wall's type: `param_set {"ids":["<wall id>"],"key":"@type","value":"Block 190 Core-filled"}` answered `{"changed":1,"elements":1}`; `op:set ... key=Type` is refused. A new type: `type_duplicate`, `type_set` first.
- split wall, trim, extend, align, parallel wall, move, copy, mirror, pin, delete: `op:delete`, `op:move`.
- floor, slab: `op:add floor`. Route: ops_run `op:add floor boundary=(0,0) (8400,0) (8400,8400) (0,8400) level="Level 1" type="Concrete Slab 200 + Tile"`; a sketch is step `ribbon:Structure:Floor`, picks round the outline, then `contextual:Finish` (part 5).
- sloping floor: `Slope Arrow`, `Span Direction`, `Add Point`, `Add Split Line`, `Modify Sub Elements`, `Pick Supports`, `Reset Shape`. A floor from `op:add floor` comes out flat.
- ceiling, suspended ceiling: `op:add ceiling`, `draw-ceiling`, `Sketch Ceiling`, `Edit Boundary (ceiling)`, `Ceilings/Slope Arrow`, `draw-ceiling-rcp`. Route: ops_run `op:add ceiling boundary=(0,0) (8000,0) (8000,6000) (0,6000) level="Level 1" height=2500`.
- stair, staircase: `op:add stair`. Route: ops_run `op:add stair from=(0,0) to=(6000,0) level=Ground top="Level 1" width=1200`.
- L-shaped, U-shaped, winder, spiral, sketch stair, riser, going, ramp, switchback: `draw-stair`, `draw-stair-settings` (dialog `Stair`; reference: `Stair Settings`), `Edit Stairs`, `draw-ramp`, `draw-ramp-settings` (dialog `Ramp`). A spiral takes two points, plan in front: `commands_run {"name":"draw-stair","options":{"Shape":"spiral","Width":1000,"Inner Radius":200,"Sweep":360,"Level":"Ground","Multistorey Top Level":"Level 1"},"points":[[4000,14000],[5200,14000]],"finish":true}`; the first point is the centre, the second sets where it starts.
- railing, balustrade, handrail: `op:add railing`, `Railing`. Route: ops_run `op:add railing points=(0,5000) (6000,5000) (6000,8000) level=Ground`; on a stair `op:add railing host=<stair id>` (no level=) answers two rails.
- room, area, space, zone, room tag: `op:add room`, `Room`, `Room Separator`, `Room Tag`, `Area Boundary`, `Area (area plan)`, `views-areas`, `Space`, `Zone`, `Measure Area`. Route: `op:add tag id=<id> view=<plan id> leader=no`.

Look it up: commands_list {"tab":"Structural"}, {"tab":"Architecture"}; get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > draw-stair"}; params_schema {"category":"Walls"} (also Floors). Steps: part 5.

### Roofs, openings, doors, windows and curtain walls (gable, hip, dormer, skylight, fascia, gutter, mullion, facade, glazing)
- gable roof, gable end, rake, eaves overhang: `Roof` (options `Overhang`, `Defines Slope`, `Extend to wall core`). Four steps, walls picked round the loop; first step: `ribbon:Architecture:Roof · picks (34000,20000) · keys — · fields Options Strip: Draw=Pick Walls; Defines Slope=yes; Overhang=400 · expect —`; full call: part 14 (Recipes), recipe (s). Picture: a gable. Lift: the roof's base is its eave edge, out at the overhang: lift by the wall height less Overhang x tan(Slope). Overhang 400, Slope 35: Base Offset 2700 stood about 280 mm above 2700 walls; 2500 sat on them with no gap seen. `commands_list {"name":"Gable"}` answered `count: 0`.
- roof from a drawn outline: `commands_run {"name":"Roof","points":[[30000,20000],[38000,20000],[38000,25000],[30000,25000],[30000,20000]],"finish":true}`.
- hip roof, flat roof, roof deck, parapet roof: `add roof`. `op:add roof boundary=(0,0) (8000,0) (8000,6000) (0,6000) level="Level 1" slope=45`; no `slope` = hip of 30 degrees; `slope=0` = flat. Later: `op:move id=<roof id> by=(0,0,2700)` (the wall height; less with an overhang), `op:set id=<roof id> key=Slope value=35`
- dormer, roof hole, rooflight hole, skylight: `Roof Cut-out` (button Dormer, step `ribbon:Architecture:Dormer`) is a sketch tool; `commands_list {"name":"Dormer"}` finds it and `Skylight` answered `count: 0`; the Dormer step with five picks closing a rectangle and `Draw=Line` pressed the tool and UNION said `cannot proceed: no roof under the click to host the dormer on`, then `contextual:Finish` answered `cannot proceed: sketch has no loops`.
- roof truss, king post, rafter, purlin, ridge beam: `Truss`, `Edit Profile (truss)`, `Attach Top/Bottom`, `Framing Layout`. Rafter: `op:add beam`, `op:set id=<beam> key="Start Level Offset" value=1200`
- roof build-up, tile, metal deck, green roof: `type_set` key `Layer <n> Material` on every layer (Realistic draws the structure layer's). A roof's type changes with `param_set` key `@type`, as a wall's does.
- door, window, doorway: `add door`, `add window`. `op:add door wall=<wall id> at=(2000,0)`; `op:add window wall=<wall id> at=(5000,6000) sill=900 type="1800 x 1800"`. One of `at=` or `offset=`; wall id from the wall line's `made`; `flip=yes`, `hand=yes`.
- door or window by click: `Door`, `Window`. `ribbon:Architecture:Door · picks (2000,0) · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect Doors +1`; `ribbon:Structure:Opening:Window · picks (5000,6000) · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect Windows +1`.
- library door block, door colour: `op:place block ... host=<wall>` cuts no opening; `op:add door wall=<wall id> at=(x,y) type=<type>` cuts it. Colour: `op:set id=<id,id> key=Material value="<file material>"`.
- door schedule, repeat windows per floor: `schedule_read {"view":"Door Schedule","limit":50}`; `op:array id=<window id> count=18 step=(0,0,3600)`.
- curtain wall, glass facade, storefront: a wall of a Function-Curtain type (`Exterior Glazing`, `Storefront`; template `Curtain Wall` is not glass). `commands_list {"name":"Curtain Wall"}` answered `count: 0` too. Glass-wall calls: part 4 (Fast ops), piece "Materials and types". Grid and panels come with the wall.
- mullion, glazing bar: `Mullion`, one step per face: `ribbon:Architecture:Mullion · picks (16800,25200) · keys Escape Escape · fields Options Strip: Place On=All Grid Lines · expect —`

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"Architecture"}`, `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > Roof"}`, `params_schema {"category":"Roofs"}`. Draw modes and steps: part 5.

### Freeform curves and surfaces, masses and solid forms (NURBS, spline, loft, sweep, revolve, panels, control points, dome, canopy)
UNION has NURBS curves (element `Freeform Curve`) and NURBS surfaces (element `Form`); `commands_list {"name":"NURBS"}` and `{"name":"Spline"}` answered `count: 0`. `commands_list {"tab":"Structural"}` files `Freeform Curve`, `Loft`, `Sweep`, `Revolve`, `Column on Form`, `Brace on Form` under panel Form; `{"tab":"Freeform"}` lists the rest. A plan view in front is the played route. Worked surface: part 14 (Recipes), recipe (p).

- spline, NURBS curve, curve through points, control-point curve, rail, profile: `Freeform Curve`. Route: `commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"3","Interpolate":true},"points":[[0,0],[3000,1500],[6000,-1000],[9000,800],[12000,0]],"finish":true}` (the first play sent each point with a third number 0, `[0,0,0]`; two-number points were played with other coordinates). `Degree` 1, 2 or 3; `Interpolate` false = control points; `Level`, `Offset` set the height (a point's z does not).
- loft, skin, surface through sections, tower form, vase: `Loft`. Route: `selection_set {"ids":["<curve 1>","<curve 2>","<curve 3>"]}`, then `commands_run {"name":"Loft"}` (curves in order).
- sweep, pipe along a path, rail and section, handrail form: `Sweep`. Route: `selection_set` the rail curve then the section curve, `commands_run {"name":"Sweep"}`.
- revolve, lathe, dome, surface of revolution: `Revolve`. Route: `selection_set {"ids":["<profile curve>"]}`, `commands_run {"name":"Revolve","options":{"Angle":360},"points":[[20000,-2000],[20000,2000]],"finish":true}` (the points are the axis; without them no Form is written).
- panels on a curved surface, diamond or hex facade: `Form Panels`. `selection_set {"ids":["<form id>"]}`, `commands_run {"name":"Form Panels"}` made 240 `Curtain Panels`. The tool stays standing: `steps_run {"steps":["chrome:Canvas Zoom to Fit · picks — · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect —"]}`.
- colour of a Form: `op:set id=<form id> key=Material value="Play White"` (after `op:add material name="Play White"`): a plain colour material showed in the Realistic view. Blocks, doors and windows take a texture through their Material row (part 7).
- read a form back: `element_get {"id":"<id>"}` gives Form rows `Control Net U`, `Control Net V`, `Material`; Freeform Curve rows `Degree`, `Control Points`, `Interpolate`. `document_info {"categories":true}` counts `Form`.
- model line, 3D line, circle or arc or ellipse in the model, spline line, 3D lettering: Spline: `steps_run {"steps":["ribbon:Setout:Model Line · picks (50000,12000) (52000,13500) (54000,11000) (56000,12500) · keys Return Escape Escape · fields Options Strip: Draw=Spline · expect —"]}`
- curved wall, circular floor, elliptical slab, spline outline: `Wall: Architectural` (step `ribbon:Architecture:Wall`) with `Draw=Start-End-Radius Arc`.
- ALBATROSS curve and surface cards: Curve (Line, Polyline, Arc, Circle, Divide, Offset, Join, Evaluate), Surface (Extrude, Loft, Surface Divide, Surface Points, Boundary), Intersect (Curve with Plane, Solid with Plane). Route: `albatross_place {"kind":"Polyline"}`, `albatross_wire`, `albatross_set`.

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"Freeform"}`, `commands_list {"name":"Loft"}` (two commands answer), `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > Freeform Curve"}`, `params_schema {"category":"Reference Points"}`. Picture of a Form: `view_camera {"fit":true,"azimuth":125,"pitch":-24}` (part 6).

### Structure: columns, beams, braces, trusses, foundations, reinforcement, loads and analysis (footing, rebar, steel, concrete, connection, slab)

- grid, level, storey, model line, spline line: `Gridline`, `Storey`, `3D Line`. Route: `op:add grid from=(0,-2000) to=(0,12000) name=A`; `op:add level elevation=3000 name="Level 2"`. Spline: `ribbon:Setout:Model Line` with `fields Options Strip: Draw=Spline` and `keys Return Escape Escape`; full call: part 14 (Recipes), recipe (t).
- column, post, raking column: `Column`. Route: `op:add column at=(0,0) level=Ground type=310UC158`.
- beam, girder, joist, purlin, sloped beam: `Framing`. Route: `op:add beam from=(0,0) to=(8400,0) level="Level 1" type=530UB82.0`; slope: `op:set id=<beam> key="Start Level Offset" value=1200`, same for `End Level Offset`.
- slab, deck, sloped slab, slab edge: `Floor: Structural`, `Slab Edge`, `Span Direction`. Route: `op:add floor boundary=(0,0) (8400,0) (8400,8400) (0,8400) level="Level 1" type="Concrete Slab 200 + Tile"`.
- structural wall, shear wall, plinth, reveal: `Wall: Structural`, `Wall Sweep`, `Wall Reveal`. Route: `ribbon:Structure:Wall · picks (0,0) (8000,0) (8000,6000) (0,6000) (0,0) · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect Walls +4`; its key presses `Wall`.
- change section, structural material: `type_duplicate`, `type_set`. Route: `type_set {"category":"Structural Framing","type":"323.9x10CHS","family":"Circular Hollow Section - Hot-Finished","key":"Material","value":"Stainless Steel Brushed"}`.
- UB, UC, CHS, RHS, glulam, bored pile: families `Universal Beam`, `Bored Pile`. Place by `op:place block` (part 8, Blocks).
- structural plan, schedule, tag, dimensions: `op:add view kind=structural level=Ground name="Column Setting-Out Plan"`; `op:add schedule category="Structural Columns" fields=Type,Count,Length name="Column Schedule by Type" itemize=no`; `Tag All`, `annotate-autodim`.
- NURBS, loft, sweep, revolve: `Freeform Curve`, `Loft`, `Sweep`, `Revolve`, `Column on Form`, `Brace on Form`. Loft: `selection_set` the curves, then `commands_run {"name":"Loft"}`; full call: part 14 (Recipes), recipe (p).
- gridshell, diagrid, lattice: ALBATROSS `Brace between Points`, `Series`, `Expression`. Route: `albatross_place {"kind":"Brace between Points","at":[960,160]}`, wire, set `run` true.

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"Structural"}`, `library_list {"category":"Structural Framing"}`, `params_schema {"category":"Structural Framing"}`, `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > Rebar"}`. Detail: parts 4 (Fast ops), 5 (Commands), 9 (Forms), 10 (ALBATROSS).

### Building services: ducts, pipes, cable trays, conduit, equipment, fixtures and systems (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, lighting, sprinkler, mechanical, clash check)

- duct, HVAC, supply air, return air, exhaust: `Duct` (op add duct). Route: `ribbon:Systems:Duct · picks (1000,1000) (5000,1000) · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect Ducts +1`; sized: `fields Options Strip: Width=300; Height=150; Middle Elevation=2700; System Type=Return Air`.
- diffuser, grille, air handling unit, boiler, thermostat: `Diffuser` (op add terminal), `Plant Item` (op add equipment), `Mechanical Control Device` (Type). Route: `ribbon:Systems:Air Terminal · picks (3000,1000) · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect Air Terminals +1` on a duct. Ceiling diffuser: `op:place block family="<family>" at=(3000,1000) level=Ground host=<ceiling id>`, the id from `elements_query {"category":"Ceilings","fields":["id","type"],"limit":100}`; part 8 (Blocks), piece "Place a block". A duct runs below it, under the ceiling height.
- count, resize, repeat per floor: `document_info {"categories":true}`.

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"Services"}`, `library_list {"category":"Mechanical Equipment"}`, `params_schema {"category":"Ducts"}`, `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > Duct"}`. Detail: part 4 (Fast ops), 5 (Commands, steps and dialogs), 10 (ALBATROSS).

### Views: plans, sections, elevations, callouts, 3D views, drafting views, legends, filters and view templates (visibility, hide, isolate, crop, scope box, view range, detail level, scale)

Views tab. Step: `key · picks · keys · fields · expect`; empty part —.

- display style, wireframe, shaded, Realistic, shadows: `Display Options`. `steps_run {"steps":["ribbon:View:Display Options · picks — · keys — · fields Display Options: Style=Realistic; Show Edges=no; Silhouette Edges=no; Shadows=yes; Soft Shadows=yes; Backdrop=Sky; OK= · expect —"]}`. Full call: part 14 (Recipes), recipe (n). `commands_run {"name":"Shaded"}` sets Display Style to Shaded.
- 3D view, isometric, orbit: `Model View` (`{3D}` in `view_activate`; id `view-3d`). `view_activate {"view":"{3D}"}`, `view_camera {"fit":true,"azimuth":125,"pitch":-24}`. `op:add 3d view`.
- cutaway, section box: `Clip Box`. `selection_set` the elements, then `commands_run {"name":"Clip Box"}`; off: `op:set id=view-3d key="Section Box" value=no`.
- view rows, scale, detail level: `element_get {"id":"view-3d"}` reads. `op:set id=<view id> key=Scale value=1:200`, `op:set id=<view id> key="Detail Level" value=Coarse` write.
- floor plan, structural plan, RCP: `Plans`. `op:add view kind=plan level="Level 8" name="Level 8 Plan"` (kind plan, structural, ceiling); step `ribbon:View:Plan Views › Floor Plan`. Floor and ceiling plans share a name: `view_activate` refuses it with `cannot proceed: 2 views answer to 'Ground': ...; name the one wanted by its id`, and an op's `view=` takes the floor plan; send the id from `views_list`.
- section, elevation: `Section`, `Elevation`. `op:add section from=(50000,-2000) to=(56000,-2000) depth=8000 name="Probe Section" view=48660e38a721430d899d5d8a96df3bec`, `op:add elevation` takes `view=<id>` the same way; full call: part 14 (Recipes), recipe (m).
- auto sections, every grid: `views-autosections`. `view_activate` a plan, then `commands_run {"name":"views-autosections","options":{"Sections":true,"Elevations":true,"Sheets":true,"Grids":"all"}}`.
- drafting view, 2D detail: `2D View`, dialog `New Drafting View`. `op:add drafting view name="Roof Junction" scale=1:10`.
- duplicate view: `Copy View`. `view_activate` the plan, then `commands_run {"name":"Copy View"}`.
- hide category: `op:set view view="Level 8 Plan" hide="Structural Framing,Structural Columns"`; also `show=`, `map=plain:lightgrey`. 3D level and grid lines: `op:set view view=view-3d hide=Levels,Grids`.
- view filter: `View Filters`. Once `steps_run {"steps":["view-filters:add:Braces:Structural Framing;Structural Usage;equals;Other:hide=1 · picks — · keys — · fields — · expect —"]}`, then per open plan `view-filters:apply:Braces`.
- list, open, delete views, zoom, tabs: `views_list {"kind":"Floor Plan"}`, `view_activate {"view":"<floor plan id>"}` (see floor plan, above), `op:delete id=<view id>`.
- picture, put on sheet, crop: `view_image {"window":"main"}`. `op:place view view="Level 8 Plan" sheet=A104 at=(115,140)`, add `scale=1:200 crop=(x0,y0) (x1,y1)`.

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"View"}`, `commands_list {"name":"<name>"}`, `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > <name>"}`. Detail: parts 6, 14 (m).

### Annotation: dimensions, text, tags, keynotes, symbols, detail lines and filled regions (hatch, leader, note, spot level, insulation, revision cloud)

Detailing tab (door tab `Annotate`, 51 commands). Drawn in one plan, section, elevation or drafting view. Step: `key · picks · keys · fields · expect`; empty part —.

- text, note: `Text` (options Type, Scale, Height, List, Leader). `op:add text at=(0,-10) view="General Notes" text="1. All dimensions are in millimetres."`.
- leader: `ribbon:Annotate:Text · picks (145,-500) (500,-500) · keys S T U D Space 1 4 5 Return Escape · fields Options Strip: Leader=on · expect Text Notes +1`; first pick is the arrow tip.
- dimension, aligned: `Aligned`. `ribbon:Annotate:Aligned · picks (0,-800) (145,-800) (72,-950) · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect Dimensions +1`; picks on element ends, the third places.
- dimension string, dimension all: `op:add dimension chain points=(0,-1000) (8400,-1000) (16800,-1000) view=<plan id> offset=-3000` (points on live elements); `view_activate` the plan first; `commands_run {"name":"annotate-autodim"}` dimensions a whole plan.
- tag, door tag, mark: `Tag`. `op:add tag id=<element id> view=<plan id> leader=no`. Tag all: `view_activate` the plan, then `commands_run {"name":"Tag All","points":[[16800,12600]]}` with ONE point; if the door stays busy, `chrome:Canvas Zoom to Fit · picks — · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect nothing selected`.
- north arrow, scale bar, tolerance: `op:add symbol at=(-9000,30000) view=<plan id>`.
- detail line, rectangle, circle, arc, spline: `2D Line`. `ribbon:Annotate:Detail Line › Rectangle · picks (0,-800) (145,-90) · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect Lines +4`. `op:add detail line points=(x,y) (x,y) view=<view>`; modes Circle, Ellipse, Spline, Pick Lines, Inscribed Polygon, Start-End-Radius Arc: `fields Options Strip: Draw=<mode>` in its ribbon step, part 14 (Recipes), recipe (t): Wall and Model Line.
- hatch, filled region, masking region: `Hatch`. `ribbon:Annotate:Region › Filled Region · picks (-60,-800) (0,-800) (0,-90) (-60,-90) (-60,-800) · keys — · fields — · expect nothing selected`, then `contextual:Finish · picks — · keys — · fields — · expect Filled Regions +1`.
- insulation, batt: `ribbon:Annotate:Insulation · picks (72,-780) (72,-100) · keys Escape Escape · fields Options Strip: Width=100 · expect Detail Items +1`.
- read back: `elements_query {"category":"Dimensions","limit":50}`, `document_info {"categories":true}`.

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"Annotate"}`, `commands_list {"name":"<name>"}`, `get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > <name>"}`. Detail: part 14 (e), (m).

### Blocks, materials, textures and the material node graph (family, furniture, plants, trees, brick, timber, glass, paint, colour, variation, repeat)
Blocks, types, Block Editor, materials, 67 photograph texture sets, Material cards.

- texture on a block, door, window: the element's `Material` row. `ops_run {"lines":["op:set id=<id>,<id> key=Material value=\"<file material>\""]}`. One texture per element. A Structural Framing block: set the material on its type. With no Material, Furniture and Doors draw grey wood grain: use a plain material (`render_colour` #ffffff, `glow` 0.2); recipe (o) of part 14 (Recipes).
- new material, colour, paint, metal, bump, glow: `ops_run {"lines":["op:add material name=\"X\"","op:set material name=\"X\" key=render_colour value=#7E9AAE"]}`. Keys that reach the Realistic view: texture, texture_size, texture_rotation, render_colour, roughness, metallic, bump, transparency, glow. A wrong key lists the 33 keys a material keeps.
- photo texture, brick, timber, concrete, steel, stone, roof tile, lawn, repeat, tiling: 67 sets, photographs in their own colours. `op:add material library=<set> name="X"`. A large wall or lawn shows the texture's tile; `texture_size` (mm) sets it (part 7). Nine sets (names: part 7) draw brightness only: give `render_colour`. Your own set: part 7.
- glass, see-through, wall, floor, roof finish, layers, beam material: `op:set material name="Facade Glass" key=transparency value=0.6` (transparency runs 0 to 1); `type_duplicate {"category":"Walls","type":"Exterior Glazing","name":"Blue-grey glass"}`; `types_list` reads layers. A layer's material: `type_set {"category":"Walls","type":"Generic 200mm","key":"Layer 1 Material","value":"Play White"}` answers the type's `layers`; recipe (o). The STRUCTURE layer is drawn: set every layer.
- change type, retype: `param_set {"ids":["<id>"],"key":"@type","value":"<type name from types_list>"}` answered `{"changed":1,"elements":1}` on a wall and a roof. `op:set id=<id> key=Type` is refused (`A Roof has no parameter 'Type'`). A wall on a new type: `type_duplicate`, `type_set` Layer n Material, `param_set` `@type`.
- place a block, furniture, tree, steel section: `op:place block family="<name>" type=<type> at=(0,-20000) level=Ground rotation=0`; ceiling-hung: `host=<ceiling id>`; an unknown category answers 'load it first'.
- door, window in a wall (cuts the opening): `op:add door wall=<wall id> at=(2000,0)`, `op:add window wall=<wall id> at=(5000,6000)`; tools `Door`, `Window`. `place block ... host=<wall id>` cuts no opening.
- block colour per part, fabric, leather: about 67 material words (Paint - White, Melamine, Leather, Foliage). `type_set` on the block type, key its material parameter. Another word falls to pale timber.
- block instance parameter: `op:set id=<id> key=Length value=<v>` (part 8).
- find a block, library, list placed: `library_list {"category":"Furniture","limit":5}` answers `count`, `more`, `names`, `next`, `total` (204); `library_list {}` answers `library.list needs a category`.
- steel section type: place its block once, `op:delete` the made id; the type stays.
- hatch, fill pattern, object styles: `steps_run {"steps":["ribbon:Manage:Additional Settings › Fill Patterns · picks — · keys Return · fields Fill Patterns: Patterns=Gravel · expect dialog closed"]}`, `ribbon:Manage:Object Styles` (fields Object Styles: Categories=<name>).
- Materials window, IFC materials, procedural texture, import mesh: `Materials`, `IFC Materials`, `render-textures`, `Unpack Import`; Import is the person's press.
- node graph, shader, PBR, normal map, weathering, relief: `albatross_place {"kind":"Real-World Size"}`, `albatross_set`, `albatross_wire`, `albatross_graph`, `albatross_delete`. Cards: Real-World Size, Base Colour Map, Normal Map, Roughness Map, Height Map, AO Map, Multiply Map, Flatten Normal, Shading Colour, Surface Pattern, Cut Pattern, Pattern Colour, Relief, Rock Scatter, Dirt, Edge Wear, Moss and Stain, Wetness, Material Output. Place and wire.

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"Make"}`, `params_schema {"category":"<category>"}`, `types_list {"category":"<category>"}`, `library_list {"category":"<category>"}`; `get_guide {"part":"guide > 7"}` (Materials), `guide > 8`, `guide > 10`.

### Change and select: move, copy, rotate, mirror, array, align, trim, join, group, filter and measure (offset, split, extend, pin, delete, undo, redo, scale, stretch, change type, swap type)

- delete, remove, erase, undo, redo, take back: `Delete`, op `delete`. `ops_run {"lines":["op:delete id=<id,id>"]}`. `steps_run {"steps":["qa:Undo · picks — · keys — · fields — · expect —"]}` takes back your newest call; `qa:Redo · picks — · keys — · fields — · expect —` redoes it; the short `qa:Undo · expect —` is played too.
- array, repeat, pattern: op `array`. `op:array id=<seed> count=5 step=(8400,0,0)`.

- many changes, node graph: `ops_run`; `batch` makes one undo entry, method names carry a dot (`selection.set`, `param.set`, `commands.run`; full call: part 5, batch).

Look it up: `commands_list {"tab":"Modify"}`, `commands_list {"name":"Break"}` (`{"name":"Level","brief":true}` answered `Storey`; `count: 0` is no missing feature), `get_guide {"part":"reference > Ops grammar"}`; part 4.

## 4. Fast ops: one line per element (the quick route, not the limit)
In this part: every op kind with its keys. Pieces: the call and its answer; value forms; levels, grids, walls, floors, ceilings, rooms, shafts; roofs, stairs, railings, fascias, gutters; columns, beams, braces; doors, windows, blocks; services; views and sections; sheets, schedules, printing; annotation; materials and types; change, move, copy, array, delete; facts met in play. Ops are the quick route. A thing with no op line is reached with `commands_run` or a ribbon step (part 5, Commands, steps and dialogs) after a look-up in part 2 (Find any control).

An op line is `op:<verb> <kind> key=value ...`. `ops_run` takes up to 500 lines as ONE Undo step; on a large model send 25 to 35. Units are mm and degrees; points are model x, y. A wrong kind is answered with the list of the kinds. A real call and its answer:

    ops_run {"name":"play: material on forms","lines":["op:set id=0da7758bd7bcd48999b9b0359b180785 key=Material value=\"Play White\"","op:set id=3e554d07689842945392daad3f37a354 key=Material value=\"Play White\""]}
    {"results":[{"changed":["0da7758bd7bcd48999b9b0359b180785"],"line":1,"ok":true,"rows":1,"state":"changed"},{"changed":["3e554d07689842945392daad3f37a354"],"line":2,"ok":true,"rows":1,"state":"changed"}],"undo":"Add-in: play: material on forms"}

Look it up:

    commands_list {"name":"Freeform Curve"}

### The ops_run call, its answer, batches and Undo

Every line starts with `op:`.

Five lines and the whole answer:

    ops_run {"name":"play: materials 2","lines":["op:add material library=copper name=\"Play Copper\"","op:add material library=zinc_cladding name=\"Play Zinc\"","op:set id=3e554d07689842945392daad3f37a354 key=Material value=\"Play Copper\"","op:set id=3f9108493f1e01717395b83138b70760 key=Material value=\"Play Zinc\"","op:add floor boundary=(-6000,-18000)(30000,-18000)(30000,14000)(-6000,14000) level=\"Ground\""]}
    {"results":[{"line":1,"made":["Play Copper"],"ok":true,"rows":3,"state":"changed"},{"line":2,"made":["Play Zinc"],"ok":true,"rows":3,"state":"changed"},{"changed":["3e554d07689842945392daad3f37a354"],"line":3,"ok":true,"rows":1,"state":"changed"},{"changed":["3f9108493f1e01717395b83138b70760"],"line":4,"ok":true,"rows":1,"state":"changed"},{"line":5,"made":["floor-4083a1d163c3bee6"],"ok":true,"rows":2,"state":"changed"}],"undo":"Add-in: play: materials 2"}

Read each result:
- Its reply is `ops.run` in the reference. A material's id is its name. A `delete` answers the id it removed in `changed`.

A refused line does not stop the lines after it. Line 1 of a four-line call answered `{"line":1,"ok":false,"state":"refused","words":"cannot proceed: the library holds no texture set named 'zinc_standing_seam'; nothing was written"}` and lines 2 to 4 were written.

A wrong word on purpose lists what exists: a refusal names its fix and the valid words (types, parameters, views, card kinds).

A wrong kind lists the kinds. `op:add gable at=(0,0)` answered:

    cannot proceed: 'gable' is not a kind of add (add column, add grid, add level, add beam, add brace, add wall, add floor, add roof, add ceiling, add material, add room, add shaft, add stair, add railing, add door, add window, add detail line, add filled region, add insulation, add view, add section, add elevation, add drafting view, add legend, add schedule, add 3d view, add sheet, place view, print sheets, set, set material, set view, set element graphics, delete, delete sheet, remove view, move, add duct, add pipe, add terminal, add equipment, add duct system, add fascia, add gutter, add text, add dimension, add dimension chain, add tag, add symbol, place block, copy, rotate, mirror, array)

Batches:
- On a large model send 25 to 35 lines a call.
- A row of identical members is one `array` line (piece "Change, move, copy, mirror, array and delete").
- One drawing call at a time. `another AI chat's drawing call is still running in UNION; retry in a moment` is not a failure: send the call again.
- Every write rebuilds the 3D view. Write with a plan view in front (`view_activate` a floor plan); part 6 (See your work) shows the 3D view once.

Ids in angle brackets come from the `made` of an earlier line.

### Value forms: point, points, polygon, pair, heading, slope, vector, count, ids and the rest

| Form | Written as | Example |
|---|---|---|
| point | (x,y) in mm: two numbers | `(1000,2000)` |
| heading | (x,y) in mm: the point the run heads toward; the answer's note names where it ends | `(6000,0)` |
| points | (x,y) (x,y) ... in mm: two points or more | `(0,0) (4000,0) (4000,3000)` |
| pair | (x,y) (x,y) in mm: exactly two points | `(0,0) (4000,0)` |
| polygon | (x,y) (x,y) (x,y) ... in mm: three points or more | `(0,0) (4000,0) (4000,3000)` |
| mm | a number in mm | `1000` |
| degrees | a number in degrees | `90` |
| slope | a slope in degrees, from -89 to 89: 0 is flat | `30` |
| vector | dx,dy,dz in mm: two or three numbers | `(100,0,0)` |
| movevector | dx,dy,dz in mm: two or three numbers; the id of a placed view moves it on its sheet by dx,dy in sheet mm, y down the page (dz is 0) | `(100,0,0)` |
| sheetpoint | (x,y) in sheet mm: the placed view's frame lower-left corner, measured from the sheet's lower-left corner, y up the page | `(40,30)` |
| yesno | yes or no | `yes` |
| count | a whole number of 2 or more: the instances in all, the original included | `3` |
| ids | ids separated by commas: one or more | `a1,a2` |
| edges | roof edge numbers from 0 separated by commas: one or more | `0,1` |
| plankind | plan, structural or ceiling; sections, elevations, drafting views and 3D views are made by add section, add elevation, add drafting view and add 3d view | `plan` |
| facing | north, east, south or west | `north` |

Rules of writing:
- Separate the points of a list with a space or a comma; a space inside a point's brackets is allowed. Points written touching, `(-6000,-18000)(30000,-18000)(30000,14000)`, were read as a list too.
- A one-point key (`at`, `from`, `to`) takes one point. A second bare point after it is refused: `cannot proceed: 'column (1,1)' is not a kind of add (add column, add grid, ...)`.
- `level` is a level's name (`Ground`). `view` is a view's name or id from `views_list`. Give the id: where a floor plan and a ceiling plan share a name (`Ground`), an op's `view=` takes the floor plan (piece "Views, sections, elevations and 3D views").

### Levels, grids, walls, floors, ceilings, rooms and shafts

Every example uses the Architectural template's names (levels Ground at 0, Level 1 at 3000, Roof at 6000; a name that exists is refused).

`add level`: needs elevation (mm). May take name.
Example:

    op:add level elevation=3000 name="Level 2"

- Move or rename a template level with `set`: `op:set id="level-Level 1" key=Elevation value=3600`, then `op:set id=level-Roof key=Elevation value=7200` and `op:set id=level-Roof key=Name value="Level 2"`. The id stays `level-Roof` after the rename. `levels_list` reads levels back.
- A level made by `op:add level` gets its plan view from `add view` (piece "Views, sections, elevations and 3D views").
- The landscape pad stands at the lowest level whose name is like "Ground". Name the lowest site level so, or lower parts are buried.

`add grid`: needs from (point), to (point). May take name.
Example:

    op:add grid from=(0,-2000) to=(0,12000) name=A

A grid named with digits plays as `name=1` or `name="1"`. `grids_list` reads grids back.

`add wall`: needs from (point), to (point), level. May take type, height (mm), top, line.
Example:

    op:add wall from=(0,0) to=(8000,0) level=Ground

- One line is one wall: four walls are four lines. `made` is the wall's id.
- The top is `top` (a level name) or `height` (mm); both together are refused: `cannot proceed: add wall takes top= (a level) or height= (mm), not both`.
- `height` is the wall's own height in mm, measured from its level. A wall on Level 1 with `height=2700` starts at 3000: `op:add wall from=(50000,0) to=(56000,0) level="Level 1" height=2700` made a wall whose line reads z = 3000.
- Height and Base Offset order: piece "Facts met in play". Curtain walls and glass: piece "Materials and types".
- A curved wall is the `Wall: Architectural` tool (step `ribbon:Architecture:Wall`) with `Draw=Start-End-Radius Arc` set on the options strip inside the ribbon step that presses it; three picks: start, end, a point on the arc. Part 14 (Recipes) recipe (t).

`add floor`: needs boundary (points), level. May take type.
Example:

    op:add floor boundary=(-6000,-18000)(30000,-18000)(30000,14000)(-6000,14000) level="Ground"

- `boundary` closes itself: do not repeat the first point.
- With no `type` the floor is "Generic 300mm", 300 mm thick. Read a type's thickness from `types_list {"category":"Floors"}`: its `layers` give each layer in mm. "Concrete Slab 200 + Tile" is Ceramic 10 over Concrete 200:

        op:add floor boundary=(0,0) (8400,0) (8400,8400) (0,8400) level="Level 1" type="Concrete Slab 200 + Tile"

`add ceiling`: needs level. Exactly one of at (point), boundary (polygon). May take height (mm), type.
Example:

    op:add ceiling boundary=(0,0) (8000,0) (8000,6000) (0,6000) level="Level 1" height=2500

- `boundary` needs no walls; an outline that already holds a ceiling is refused. `height` is mm above the level; `type` a Ceilings type name. Left out, the tool's starting values stand.
- `at` works inside four walls on `level` or over a Room. A point in no walls is refused in the tool's words: `cannot proceed: no room at this point of Ground and no closed walls round it`.

`add room`: needs at (point), level. May take name, number.

`add shaft`: needs boundary (pair), level. May take top.

### Roofs, stairs, railings, fascias and gutters

`add roof`: needs boundary (polygon), level. May take type, slope (slope).
Examples:

    op:add roof boundary=(0,0) (8000,0) (8000,6000) (0,6000) level="Level 1" slope=45
    op:add roof boundary=(20000,0) (28400,0) (28400,8400) (20000,8400) level="Level 2" slope=0

- `boundary` closes itself. `type` is a Roofs type name. With no `slope` the roof is a hip of 30 degrees (Form Hip, Slope 30). `slope` sets every edge. `slope=0` makes a flat roof (Form Flat, Slope 0). `made` is the roof's id.
- Write the slope in the add line.
- The `Roof` tool (tab Architecture, panel Build; prompt "Sketch the roof footprint"; options Offset, Radius, Overhang, Defines Slope, Extend to wall core, Sides; draw modes include Pick Walls, Pick Lines, Circle, Spline) drew a roof from a closed footprint, the first point repeated to close it. It answered `Roof: 5 point(s)`:

        commands_run {"name":"Roof","points":[[30000,20000],[38000,20000],[38000,25000],[30000,25000],[30000,20000]],"finish":true}

- A gable roof is played with the Roof tool in Pick Walls mode, with `Defines Slope` set to no on the two gable-end walls. The draw mode and its options are set on the options strip inside the ribbon step that presses the tool. The first step line of the play, in a `steps_run` call:

        ribbon:Architecture:Roof · picks (34000,20000) · keys — · fields Options Strip: Draw=Pick Walls; Defines Slope=yes; Overhang=400 · expect —

  The whole call is in part 14 (Recipes) recipe (s). A draw mode set in `commands_run` is refused: `cannot proceed: Roof has no option Draw Mode; nothing was written`.
- The gable roof was made at its level. Lift a pitched roof by the wall height less overhang x tan(slope), because its base is the eave edge, out at the overhang: with Overhang 400 and Slope 35 that is 280 mm, about 2420 on 2700 walls. Base Offset 2700 stood about 280 mm above the wall tops; Base Offset 2500 sat on the walls with no gap seen. The played call lifted by the full 2700 (send less to sit on the walls); `element_get` read Base Offset 2700 and Slope 35:

        ops_run {"name":"lift roof","lines":["op:move id=<roof id> by=(0,0,2700)","op:set id=<roof id> key=Slope value=35"]}

- The dormer opening is the sketch tool `Roof Cut-out` (tab Structural, panel Opening; ribbon button Dormer, step `ribbon:Architecture:Dormer`); `commands_list {"name":"Dormer"}` answered it.
- Lofts, sweeps and revolves make freeform surfaces: part 9 (Forms, freeform curves and surfaces).

`add stair`: needs from (point), to (heading), level, top. May take type, width (mm).
Example:

    op:add stair from=(0,0) to=(6000,0) level=Ground top="Level 1" width=1200

- `from` is the start of the run, `to` the point it heads toward, not its end. `top` is the level it reaches; `type` a Stairs type name. The answer's note names the end, `the run ends at its last riser (x,y)`: read it, the run follows its risers.
- The spiral stair takes two points, the centre and then where it starts. Its call is in part 3 (The map), piece "Walls, floors, ceilings, stairs, ramps...".

`add railing`: needs nothing by itself. Exactly one of points (points), host (ids). All or none of points (points), level. May take type, level, points (points), host (ids).
Examples:

    op:add railing points=(0,5000) (6000,5000) (6000,8000) level=Ground
    op:add railing host=<stair id>

- `points` is a path of two points or more with `level`. `host` is one stair id from an `add stair` answer, with no `level`: `cannot proceed: add railing host= takes no level=: the railing follows the stair`. `made` holds the railings' ids (a stair answered two, one a side).

`add fascia`: needs roof, edges (edges). May take height (mm), thickness (mm).

`add gutter`: needs roof, edges (edges). May take height (mm), thickness (mm).

### Columns, beams, braces and structure

`add column`: needs at (point), level. May take top, type.
Example:

    op:add column at=(0,0) level=Ground type=310UC158

`top` is a level name; left out, the column stands up to the next level above. `type` is a type's name from `types_list`. The rows `Base Offset` and `Top Offset` are written after the add with `op:set`.

`add beam`: needs from (point), to (point), level. May take type, usage.
Example:

    op:add beam from=(0,0) to=(8000,0) level=Ground type=530UB82.0

`add brace`: needs from (point), to (point), level. May take top, start_offset (mm), end_offset (mm), type, usage.

- Many braces at many heights: the ALBATROSS card `Brace between Points` (part 10, ALBATROSS: cards through the door).

A height that is not a storey. A member between levels keeps its level and takes an offset from it; do not add a level for each height. Read the kind's rows with `element_get` before you add a level.
- Beam: `add beam` takes no height. Set `Start Level Offset` and `End Level Offset` (mm above the level, negative below, both 0 when added; unequal ones make a sloped beam) after the add; one line sets a whole row of beams:

        op:set id=<beam> key="Start Level Offset" value=1200
        op:set id=<beam> key="End Level Offset" value=1200

- A beam's top face stands on its level plus that end's offset, and the section hangs below it (`z Justification` is Top by default; its words are Top, Center, Origin, Bottom). A 610UB125 beam (612 deep) at Level 1 (3000) read Bottom 2388 and Top 3000; after both offsets were set to -1295 it read Bottom 1093 and Top 1705.

### Doors, windows and blocks: add door, add window, place block

Part 8 (Blocks) holds the block library, colour and texture. These are the lines.

`add door`: needs wall. Exactly one of at (point), offset (mm). May take sill (mm), type, flip (yesno), hand (yesno).
`add window`: needs wall. Exactly one of at (point), offset (mm). May take sill (mm), type, flip (yesno), hand (yesno).
Examples:

    op:add door wall=<south wall id> at=(2000,0)
    op:add window wall=<north wall id> at=(5000,6000)

- `wall` is the host wall's id, from the `made` of a wall line. `at` is a point near the wall's line; `offset` is mm (0 or more) from the wall's start to the centre of the opening. `sill` is mm, 0 or more. `type` is a Doors or Windows type the model holds. A door adds an Opening, so Doors +1 reads Openings +1.
- A door or window placed with `op:add door` or `op:add window` cuts its opening. `hand=yes` was written to put the hinge at the wall's end and `flip=yes` to swing the leaf the other way.
- Read back where it stands: `element_get {"id":"<id>"}` answers `host` (the wall) and `location` `{"point":[x,y]}`.

`place block`: needs family, at (point). May take type, level, rotation (degrees), host.
Example:

    op:place block family="Circular Hollow Section - Hot-Finished" type=323.9x10CHS at=(0,-20000) level=Ground

- `family` is a Block Database block name (`library_list {"category":"<category>"}` lists them); it loads into the model when it is not there. `library_list` needs a category; `library_list {"category":"Furniture","limit":5}` answered `{"category":"Furniture","count":5,"more":true,"names":["Armchair","Banquette Booth","Bar Stool","Bed - Bunk","Bed - Double"],"next":5,"total":204}`, and `library_list {}` answered `library.list needs a category`. A ceiling-hung block needs `host=<ceiling id>`. A block's category must be one of UNION's categories, or placing answers "load it first". A family in a model holds only the types that were placed.
- One texture for the whole block: `op:set id=<id,id,...> key=Material value="<file material>"` (piece "Materials and types"). An instance parameter (a Length on a skirting run) is written after placing with `op:set id= key= value=`.

### Services: add duct, add pipe, add terminal, add equipment, add duct system

`add duct`: needs from (point), to (point), level. May take width (mm), height (mm), diameter (mm), elevation (mm), system.

`add pipe`: needs from (point), to (point), level. May take diameter (mm), elevation (mm), system.

`add terminal`: needs at (point). At least one of level, duct. May take system.

`add equipment`: needs at (point), level. May take elevation (mm).

`add duct system`: needs members (ids). May take system, name.

### Views, sections, elevations and 3D views: add view, add section, add elevation, add drafting view, add legend, set view

Use names the model does not hold (`N Elevation`, `Cut A`) and keep the `made` id. A name a view already holds is refused, yet the line stays green and the new view keeps UNION's own name: read `words` for `was made but its name was refused`.

`add view`: needs kind (plankind), level. May take name.
Example:

    op:add view kind=plan level="Level 8" name="Level 8 Plan"

`kind` is plan, structural or ceiling; `level` is required (a level that does not exist is refused naming it). Another kind is refused: `kind= wants plan, structural or ceiling; sections, elevations, drafting views and 3D views are made by add section, add elevation, add drafting view and add 3d view`. `made` is the view's id.

`add section`: needs from (point), to (point), view. May take depth (mm), name.
Example, the plan named by its id:

    op:add section from=(50000,-2000) to=(56000,-2000) depth=8000 name="Probe Section" view=48660e38a721430d899d5d8a96df3bec

`view` is the plan the cut is made in: a view's name or its id from `views_list`. Where a floor plan and a ceiling plan share the name, as `Ground` does in the Architectural template, the op takes the floor plan; give the id to be exact. In the Architectural template the Ground floor plan's id is `48660e38a721430d899d5d8a96df3bec`. `depth` is the far clip in mm; a depth left out, or 0 or less, gives the default (a note says so). `made` is the section view's id.

`add elevation`: needs at (point), facing (facing), view. May take name.
Example, the plan named by its id:

    op:add elevation at=(53000,-6000) facing=north name="Probe Elevation" view=48660e38a721430d899d5d8a96df3bec
