Each name belongs to two commands: the Freeform one (tab `Structural`, panel `Form`) and a Block Editor one (tab `Make`, panel `Forms`). `commands_list {"name":"Loft"}` returns both. `commands_run` by name ran the Freeform one each time.

Select the curves first with `selection_set`, then run. Points do not pick curves; they are the axis of a Revolve.

Loft: a smooth surface through the curves, in the order selected:

    selection_set {"ids":["<curve 1>","<curve 2>","<curve 3>"]}
    commands_run {"name":"Loft"}

Three curves gave one `Form` with `"Control Net U":3,"Control Net V":7`. The net size depends on the points of the curves: three five-point curves at `Level` Ground with `Offset` 2400, 3400 and 2700 gave `Control Net V` 5. With nothing selected: `cannot proceed: Select the Freeform Curves to loft through, in order, then press Enter`.

Sweep: the rail curve first, then the section curve. The two curves of that play:

    commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"3","Interpolate":true},"points":[[0,-12000],[4000,-10000],[8000,-13000],[12000,-11000]],"finish":true}
    commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"2","Interpolate":false,"Level":"Ground","Offset":1500},"points":[[0,-13500],[-800,-12800],[0,-12000],[800,-11200],[0,-10500]],"finish":true}
    selection_set {"ids":["<rail curve>","<section curve>"]}
    commands_run {"name":"Sweep"}

One more `Form` was written. With nothing selected: `cannot proceed: Select the rail curve, then the section curve, then press Enter`.

Revolve: the profile curve selected, then the two points of the axis. The profile of that play, drawn with three-number points (the z numbers were not used):

    commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"3","Interpolate":true},"points":[[22000,0,0],[23500,0,1500],[22800,0,3000],[23800,0,4500],[22500,0,6000]],"finish":true}
    selection_set {"ids":["<profile curve>"]}
    commands_run {"name":"Revolve","options":{"Angle":360},"points":[[20000,-2000],[20000,2000]],"finish":true}

UNION answers `{"changed":[{"category":"Form","id":"3e554d07...","kind":"insert","table":"element"}],"text":"Revolve: 2 point(s)"}`; the Form read back `Control Net U 9, Control Net V 5`. A plan view was in front. The tool's prompt after the profile is "Click the axis start". With the profile selected and no points the call answers `Revolve: 0 point(s)` and writes nothing: give the axis points. With nothing selected: `cannot proceed: Select the profile curve to revolve, then press Enter`. The ribbon step with the profile selected only starts the tool, which then stands at "Click the axis start":

    steps_run {"steps":["ribbon:Massing & Site:Revolve · picks — · keys Return · fields — · expect —"]}

After either call, read the count and the Form; do not send the call twice:

    document_info {"categories":true}
    elements_query {"category":"Form"}

`document_info` then shows `"Form": 1`. `elements_query` answers `{"category":"Form","count":1,"more":false,"rows":[{"family":"Form","id":"0da7758b...","kind":"Form","level":"","row":7,"type":"Form"}]}`: the row's `id` is the Form's id.

Reading a Form back:

    element_get {"id":"<form id>"}
    params_schema {"category":"Form"}

`element_get` answers `"params":{"Control Net U":3,"Control Net V":7,...}` and, once set, `"Material":"Play White"`. `params_schema` lists 11 rows: Category, Family, Type, Level, GUID, Element Id, Mark, Comments, Design Option, Phase Created, Phase Demolished. The material is written with an op line (next piece).

### On a surface: Form Panels, a material on a Form

Panels on a Form:

    selection_set {"ids":["<form id>"]}
    commands_run {"name":"Form Panels"}

Answer `{"changed":[],"text":"Form Panels: 0 point(s)"}`. A `document_info` sent straight after listed no `Curtain Panels`; they were counted after the next call and the step that ends the tool (below): 240 `Curtain Panels` on the form, a 12 by 20 grid of rectangular panels in the picture. 240 is the DEFAULT 12 x 20. Read the count with `document_info {"categories":true}`.

After Form Panels play this step, which ends any standing tool:

    steps_run {"steps":["chrome:Canvas Zoom to Fit · picks — · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect —"]}

When a command name finds no heading, `commands_list {"name":"<name>"}` gives the same facts.

For many members at computed points, the ALBATROSS gridshell recipe writes braces between points: part 10 (ALBATROSS).

A material on a Form. A Form takes the element `Material` row (`element_get` then shows `"Material":"Play White"`):

    ops_run {"name":"materials","lines":["op:add material name=\"Play White\"","op:set material name=\"Play White\" key=render_colour value=#f4f1ea","op:set material name=\"Play White\" key=glow value=0.2","op:add material library=copper name=\"Play Copper\"","op:set id=<form id> key=Material value=\"Play White\""]}

A plain colour material showed in the Realistic view. `render_colour` and `glow` are among the material keys seen to change the Realistic view; a wrong key lists all 33 keys a material keeps (part 7). Blocks, doors and windows take a texture through their `Material` row (part 8). The set names are the keys of the texture library: `op:add material library=zinc_standing_seam ...` answered `cannot proceed: the library holds no texture set named 'zinc_standing_seam'; nothing was written`. Materials, texture sets and the node graph: part 7 (Materials).

### Geometry by cards: ALBATROSS Curve and Surface groups

ALBATROSS holds cards that make geometry. By the program's own list of card kinds (`albatross_place {"kind":"zzz"}` lists every kind by group): group Curve, 20 kinds (Length, Line, Polyline, Arc, Arc 3Pt, Circle, Curve, Curve Closest Point, Divide, End Points, Evaluate, Explode, Extend, Join, Offset, Point In Curve, Point On Curve, Polygon, Rectangle, Shatter); group Surface, 8 kinds (Area, Boundary, Extrude, Loft, Surface Divide, Surface Evaluate, Surface Offset, Surface Points); group Intersect, 3 kinds (Curve with Curve, Curve with Plane, Solid with Plane). The `Point` card is in the Vector group. `Point` and `Polyline` were placed and wired. Place the card and read its answer. Placing, wiring and the cards that write the model: part 10 (ALBATROSS). `Brace between Points` was played.

### A worked sequence: curves at three heights, a surface, panels, a material, a picture

The net size depends on the point count. Change the points to change the shape.

1. A floor plan in front. Take the plan's id from `views_list {}`:

        views_list {}
        view_activate {"view":"<Ground floor plan id>"}

2. Three curves at Level Ground, at heights 2400, 3400 and 2700. Keep the id from each answer:

        commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"3","Interpolate":true,"Level":"Ground","Offset":2400},"points":[[0,0],[3000,1500],[6000,-1000],[9000,800],[12000,0]],"finish":true}
        commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"3","Interpolate":true,"Level":"Ground","Offset":3400},"points":[[0,4000],[3000,6500],[6000,3500],[9000,5200],[12000,4000]],"finish":true}
        commands_run {"name":"Freeform Curve","options":{"Degree":"3","Interpolate":true,"Level":"Ground","Offset":2700},"points":[[0,8000],[3000,9000],[6000,7500],[9000,9200],[12000,8000]],"finish":true}

3. Loft them, front to back. The played loft of the three five-point curves read `Control Net U 3, Control Net V 5`:

        selection_set {"ids":["<curve 1>","<curve 2>","<curve 3>"]}
        commands_run {"name":"Loft"}
        elements_query {"category":"Form"}

4. Panels on the Form, then end the standing tool, then read the count (the played run read `"Curtain Panels": 240`):

        selection_set {"ids":["<form id>"]}
        commands_run {"name":"Form Panels"}
        steps_run {"steps":["chrome:Canvas Zoom to Fit · picks — · keys Escape Escape · fields — · expect —"]}
        document_info {"categories":true}

5. A material on the Form (the `ops_run` call in "On a surface").

6. The picture. Show the 3D view, set the Realistic look, turn the camera, picture the window (part 6 (See your work)):

        view_activate {"view":"{3D}"}
        steps_run {"steps":["ribbon:View:Display Options · picks — · keys — · fields Display Options: Style=Realistic; Show Edges=no; Silhouette Edges=no; Shadows=yes; Soft Shadows=yes; Backdrop=Sky; OK= · expect —"]}
        view_camera {"fit":true,"azimuth":125,"pitch":-24}
        view_image {"window":"main"}

Look it up (the first three `commands_list` calls, the Commands call, `params_schema` and `document_info`):

    commands_list {"name":"Freeform Curve"}
    commands_list {"name":"Loft"}
    commands_list {"tab":"Freeform"}
    get_guide {"part":"reference > Commands > Freeform Curve"}
    params_schema {"category":"Form"}
    document_info {"categories":true}

## 10. ALBATROSS: cards through the door
ALBATROSS is UNION's node graph: a canvas of cards joined by wires. A card is a small function with named inputs and outputs (its ports) and settings. An agent draws a graph with `albatross_place`, `albatross_set`, `albatross_wire` and `albatross_graph`. Some cards (28 kinds, in the Structural, Services and Model groups) write elements into the model when their `run` setting turns true: `Brace between Points` was played. The rest compute: numbers, lists, points, curves, surfaces, material maps.

In this part:
- The card tools: exact arguments, the shape of each answer, the rule for an unknown kind, a first graph, a picture of the graph.
- The card kinds by group: every kind by exact name, writers marked.
- Cards that write the model: the `run` setting, a writer's inputs, other routes to the same elements.
- A gridshell: the played recipe, 560 tubes, and a canopy graph. Then curves, surfaces and material graphs by cards, and where a material's graph is stored.

Look it up: `albatross_place {"kind":"zz no such card"}` lists every kind by group; `albatross_graph {}` lists the cards on the canvas.
Then: `view_image {"window":"albatross"}` pictures the graph; `get_guide {"part":"guide > 7. Materials"}` for materials.

### The card tools: place, set, wire, read, read one card, delete

`albatross_place` opens the ALBATROSS window when it is closed. A card is named by its `card` id from the place answer, for example `node-f3508b`, or by its drawn title. When two cards share a title, UNION takes the first. Name a card by its id.

**Place** a card:

    albatross_place {"kind":"<kind>","at":[<x>,<y>],"inputs":{"<port or setting>":<value>}}

`kind` is a library kind in any case. `at` is optional, in canvas pixels; the canvas steps the card clear of its neighbours. `inputs` is optional and sets ports and settings as `albatross_set` does. Answer: `{card, kind, title, ports:{inputs, outputs}, settings, set, refused, answer, state, messages?}`. Read `ports` and `settings` there and never guess a port name. `set` holds each input that took, read back; `refused` lists each input refused, with its words; the card stands. Both are always there, {} and [] when empty. An Expression whose formula does not parse answers `refused` and no card is placed. One canvas undo record.

`answer` is the card's answer in words. `state` is `rest`, `warning` or `error`; `messages` lists the card's own lines when `state` is `warning`. A card asking for an input is not at fault: an unwired Expression answers `cannot proceed: an Expression names an input not wired: 'x'` (state `error`) and an unwired Polyline `cannot proceed: Polyline needs its 'points' input` (state `warning`).

**An unknown kind lists the library's kinds**:

    albatross_place {"kind":"zz no such card"}

Answer: `cannot proceed: the Albatross library has no card kind 'zz no such card'. Kinds by group: Model: Beam, Brace, Column, ...` and every kind of every group, about 3 KB. Nothing is placed.

**Set** one input or setting:

    albatross_set {"card":"<card id>","input":"<port or setting>","value":<value>}

Answer: `{card, input, readBack, note?, answer, state, messages?}`. `note` says the input is wired, so the wire's value is used and the value set waits. An input the card does not carry, or a value it refuses, answers `refused` in the canvas's words; a Boolean's `state` takes `true`, `false` or the words "true" and "false". `Data Output` and `Data Input` refuse to write or read a file while UNION AI is working: the files are the person's.

**Wire** an output into an input:

    albatross_wire {"from":"<card id>","output":"<output name>","to":"<card id>","input":"<input name>"}

`output` is optional and defaults to the first output of `from`. A new wire replaces the wire already into that input (`replaced`); the same wire again answers `unchanged` true. The answer carries the `to` card's `ports`, `answer` and `state`, and `messages` if any. A cycle, or a Material pin joined to a pin of another type, is refused in the canvas's words. Any other wire stands, and the `to` card says in `answer` and `state` whether it can use the value. A card or port that is not there answers `not_found` or `refused` and names the ports it has.

**Read** the graph:

    albatross_graph {"limit":200}

Answer: `{total, count, cards:[{card, kind, title, ports:{inputs, outputs}, inputs, cut?, settings, enabled?, answer, state, messages?}], wires:[{from, output, to, input}], more, next?, stale?}`. `limit` is at most 1000; `after` is an offset. An `inputs` value over 300 characters is cut with ...; `cut` names the inputs cut. `wires` are those into the cards of the page. `enabled` is false for a disabled card only. `stale` says why the answers are not those of the graph as it stands: read again. With no window open the call opens it with the model's stored graph and no other card. The window already holds one Boolean card that is not yours.

**A first graph**: a Series (the numbers), an Expression on them, a Point from the result and a Polyline through the points. Keep the `card` id from each place answer as <S>, <E>, <P>, <L>.

    albatross_place {"kind":"series","inputs":{"count":4}}
    albatross_place {"kind":"Expression","inputs":{"expression":"x*2"}}
    albatross_place {"kind":"Point"}
    albatross_place {"kind":"Polyline"}
    albatross_wire {"from":"<S>","to":"<E>","input":"x"}
    albatross_wire {"from":"<E>","to":"<P>","input":"x"}
    albatross_wire {"from":"<P>","to":"<L>","input":"points"}
    albatross_graph {}

Ports: Series in `start`, `step`, `count`, out `numbers`; Expression in `x`, out `value`; Point in `x`, `y`, `z`, out `point`; Polyline in `points`, out `polyline`. The Series answers `[4] 0, 1, 2, 3`. When all is wired the Polyline's state is `rest`, and `albatross_graph` lists five cards and three wires. Change the count:

    albatross_set {"card":"<S>","input":"count","value":6}

**A picture of the graph**. With the ALBATROSS window open and in front, `view_image` with no `window` returns the graph, not the model. Name the window:

    view_image {"window":"albatross"}
    view_image {"window":"main"}

### The card kinds by group

UNION's own list, from the answer of `albatross_place {"kind":"zzz"}`: every group and kind, typed in any case. `*` marks the 28 cards that write elements into the model when `run` turns true (next piece). Ports of a kind are read from the place answer. Each line: the names.

- Model (21): `Beam`, `Brace`, `Column`, `Deconstruct Element`, `Filter Elements`, `Floor`, `Foundation`, `Get Parameter`, `Grid`, `Level`, `Model Pipeline`, `Move Elements`*, `Opening`, `Roof`, `Schedule from Elements`*, `Selected Elements`, `Services Run`, `Set Parameter`*, `Sheet`, `View`, `Wall`.
- Data (3): `Boolean`, `Number`, `Text`.
- Maths (25): `Addition`, `Cos`, `Division`, `Domain`, `Expression`, `Multiplication`, `Range`, `Round`, `Series`, `Sin`, `Subtraction`, `Tan`, `Average`, `Bounds`, `Construct Domain`, `Deconstruct Domain`, `Equality`, `Gate And`, `Gate Not`, `Gate Or`, `Larger Than`, `Mass Addition`, `Random`, `Remap Numbers`, `Smaller Than`.
- Sets (46): `List Length`, `Reverse`, `Clean Tree`, `Concatenate`, `Create Set`, `Cull`, `Cull Index`, `Cull Pattern`, `Dispatch`, `Duplicate Data`, `Entwine`, `Explode Tree`, `Flatten`, `Format`, `Graft`, `Insert Items`, `Key/Value Search`, `List Item`, `Member Index`, `Merge`, `Null Item`, `Partition`, `Path Mapper`, `Repeat Data`, `Replace Items`, `Replace Nulls`, `Set Difference`, `Set Intersection`, `Set Union`, `Shift`, `Shift Paths`, `Sort`, `Split List`, `Stream Filter`, `Stream Gate`, `Sub List`, `Text Case`, `Text Join`, `Text Length`, `Text Replace`, `Text Split`, `Tree Branch`, `Tree Item`, `Tree Statistics`, `Trim Tree`, `Weave`.
- Vector (28): `Array`, `Distance`, `Move`, `Point`, `Vector`, `Amplitude`, `Angle`, `Bounding Box`, `Closest Point`, `Construct Plane`, `Cross Product`, `Cull Duplicates`, `Deconstruct`, `Deconstruct Plane`, `Deconstruct Vector`, `Dot Product`, `Mirror`, `Plane`, `Populate 2D`, `Rotate`, `Scale`, `Sort Points`, `Unit Vector`, `Vector 2Pt`, `Vector Length`, `XY Plane`, `XZ Plane`, `YZ Plane`.
- Curve (20): `Length`, `Line`, `Polyline`, `Arc`, `Arc 3Pt`, `Circle`, `Curve`, `Curve Closest Point`, `Divide`, `End Points`, `Evaluate`, `Explode`, `Extend`, `Join`, `Offset`, `Point In Curve`, `Point On Curve`, `Polygon`, `Rectangle`, `Shatter`.
- Surface (8): `Area`, `Boundary`, `Extrude`, `Loft`, `Surface Divide`, `Surface Evaluate`, `Surface Offset`, `Surface Points`.
- Intersect (3): `Curve with Curve`, `Curve with Plane`, `Solid with Plane`.
- Structural (15): `Beam along Line`*, `Brace between Points`*, `Column at Point`*, `Floor from Loop`*, `Grid from Line`*, `Level from Number`*, `Opening at Point`*, `Pad at Point`*, `Raft from Loop`*, `Section by Name`, `Space from Loop`*, `Stair between Levels`*, `Strip along Curve`*, `Truss between Points`*, `Wall along Curve`*.
- Material (19): `AO Map`, `Base Colour Map`, `Cut Pattern`, `Dirt`, `Edge Wear`, `Flatten Normal`, `Height Map`, `Material Output`, `Moss and Stain`, `Multiply Map`, `Normal Map`, `Pattern Colour`, `Real-World Size`, `Relief`, `Rock Scatter`, `Roughness Map`, `Shading Colour`, `Surface Pattern`, `Wetness`.
- Services (12): `Board at Point`*, `Circuit from Devices`*, `Device at Point`*, `Duct along Polyline`*, `Fitting at Corner`*, `Fixture at Point`*, `Pipe along Polyline`*, `Riser between Levels`*, `Size from Number`, `Sprinkler at Point`*, `Terminal at Point`*, `Tray along Polyline`*.
- Params (23): `Boolean Toggle`, `Button`, `Cluster`, `Colour Swatch`, `Control Knob`, `Curve Param`, `Data Dam`, `Data Input`, `Data Output`, `Data Recorder`, `Digit Scroller`, `Gradient`, `Graph Mapper`, `Line Param`, `MD Slider`, `Panel`, `Param Viewer`, `Point Param`, `Relay`, `Scribble`, `Timer`, `Value List`, `Vector Param`.
- Display (4): `Colour Hue`, `Colour RGB`, `Custom Preview`, `Split ARGB`.

Everyday word to group: column, beam, wall, floor, slab, grid, level, stair, footing, truss, brace go to Structural; duct, pipe, sprinkler, socket, switchboard, cable tray, luminaire go to Services; formula, sequence, random, average to Maths; list, tree, text, unique to Sets; point, vector, plane, rotate to Vector; spline, polyline, arc, offset, divide to Curve; loft, extrude, surface area to Surface; slider, toggle, note, colour picker to Params; texture, normal map, roughness, weathering to Material. A kind not found by a word: send the wrong kind above and read the list.

### Cards that write the model

A writer card makes elements in the model when its `run` turns true. They are in the Structural, Services and Model groups and marked `*` in the previous piece.

**The run rule.** A writer card writes only when its `run` setting goes from false to true; played with the Brace:

    albatross_set {"card":"<card id>","input":"run","value":true}

The answer says what was made, for example `created N braces`; the made elements stand in their category (the Brace: Structural Framing; check with `document_info {"categories":true}`). Played with the Brace: the write is one Undo entry named `Add-in: albatross.set`. One Undo takes the whole write back and one Redo brings it back. The step that does it:

    steps_run {"steps":["qa:Undo · picks — · keys — · fields — · expect —"]}

After an Undo the card still reads `run` true: set `run` false, then true, to write again. `run` true again on unchanged cards answers `unchanged: 1 element already written` and adds nothing. Without `run` true a writer only previews. Cards read `level` as a level NAME; empty means the lowest level. A point that carries a z stands at that height.

**Structural writers**; input names:
- `Brace between Points`: start, end, type, run.

**Other routes to the same elements**: the `Roof` command (part 3); Forms by `Freeform Curve`, `Loft`, `Sweep` and `Revolve` (part 9). A writer card's `run` is the door's write. A `Tower` card is not among the kinds UNION lists.

### A gridshell: a lattice of tubes round a form

The card `Brace between Points` writes one steel member from a start point to an end point when its setting `run` is true, so a gridshell is a Series that counts the members, Expressions that turn the count into two points each, and one Brace card. Played, a lattice of 14 rows by 40 round, 560 members. N is the number round, M the rows, H the height, `c` the member's number.
1. Put the tube section in the file once:

        ops_run {"lines":["op:place block family=\"Circular Hollow Section - Hot-Finished\" type=323.9x10CHS at=(0,-20000) level=Ground"]}

   then `op:delete id=<the made id>`; the type stays and the Brace can use it.
2. `albatross_place` every card first, then wire (an Expression placed before its names are wired answers `cannot proceed`: expected). Cards: a Series (`start` 0, `step` 1, `count` N*M), and Expressions. `ts`, `zs` and the rest below are YOUR labels for what each holds, not names the door knows: keep each place reply's `card` id under its label and wire by that id, never by the title "Expression" (eight share it). Played with N 40, M 14, H 51200 (all 12 place calls: Two Towers Prompt 8):

        albatross_place {"kind":"Series","at":[40,150],"inputs":{"start":0,"step":1,"count":560}}

   - `ts` t at the member's start: `6.283185307179586*(c % N)/N`; `te` at its end: `6.283185307179586*((c % N) + 1)/N` (grammar `+ - * / // % **`, brackets, `sin cos tan sqrt exp floor ceil fabs pow atan2 hypot` and more; `min`, `max`, a condition and `pi` are not among them).
   - `zs` start height: `H*((c // N) + ((c % N) + (c // N)) % 2)/M`; `ze` end height: `H*((c // N) + 1 - ((c % N) + (c // N)) % 2)/M`. Neighbouring members rise and fall in turn, so they close into diamonds.
   - `xs`, `ys`, `xe`, `ye`: centre plus radius times `cos(t)` or `sin(t)`; the radius may depend on `z`, so wire `zs` (and `ze`) into them too. A plan that swells and flares, played: `R(t,z) = pow(pow(fabs(cos(t)/a),6) + pow(fabs(sin(t)/b),6), -0.16666666666666666) + 1500*(1 + sin(2*t + 4.71238898*z/28800)) + 2500*pow(1 - z/H, 3)` (a rounded rectangle of semi-axes a and b, a wave of 0 to 3,000 mm, a flare of 2,500 mm at the ground); it closes in over a roof when the first term is multiplied by `sqrt(1 - 0.55*pow(((z - roof) + fabs(z - roof))/(2*(H - roof)), 2))` (`roof` is the roof level's elevation in mm; played: H 51,200, roof 43,200).
   - The centre is the plan's middle and a, b are half the plan's x and y extents plus the clearance you want: the played plan is 33,600 by 25,200 (centre 16,800, 12,600) with a 22,400 and b 17,700, which is +5,600 and +5,100; the wave adds 0 to 3,000 mm and the flare 0 at the top. Check the smallest gap to the facade by arithmetic before the bake.
   - two `Point` cards `ps` and `pe`, and the `Brace between Points`.
3. Wire (`output` is `numbers` for the Series, `value` for an Expression, `point` for a Point): `c` into `ts`, `te`, `zs`, `ze`; `ts` into `xs` and `ys` input `t`; `te` into `xe` and `ye`; `zs` into `xs`, `ys` and `ps` input `z`; `ze` into `xe`, `ye` and `pe` input `z`; `xs`, `ys` into `ps` inputs `x`, `y`; `xe`, `ye` into `pe`; `ps` into the Brace input `start`, `pe` into `end`. Wires answer `cannot proceed` or `refused` until the last one: expected.
4. Set the section, then run:

        albatross_set {"card":"<brace>","input":"type","value":"323.9x10CHS"}
        albatross_set {"card":"<brace>","input":"run","value":true}

   The answer says `created N braces` and the members stand in Structural Framing (`document_info {"categories":true}`). To picture the shell: part 6 (See your work); on a large model: part 12 (Large models) first.
5. After a bake: one `qa:Undo` took back the whole bake (684 members, named `Add-in: albatross.set`) and one `qa:Redo` brought it back. Leave `run` true: changing a Point-side card moves the answers and not the braces. `run` true again on unchanged cards answered `unchanged: 1 element already written` and added nothing. After a `qa:Undo` of a bake the card still reads `run` true and says the same while the model holds none: set `run` false, then true.
6. Several shells (a skin round each building, columns that flare into a canopy) are the same recipe once each, with the card set placed again (a graph of 12 cards and 20 wires per shell); an Expression's variable is an input of the same name, so wire each one; the window's own Boolean card is not yours.

**A second played graph: a canopy of 70 members**. Two Towers Prompt 11: a patch of braces over two parameters, s along (7 divisions) and t across (10 rows). It is 14 cards (a Series, ten Expressions, two Points, one Brace) and 22 wires, placed first and wired by id as above, with s and t as the Expression inputs. Its Series counts 70.

- `ss` `(c % 7)/7`; `se` `((c % 7) + 1)/7`; `ts` and `te` use `c // 7` and `c % 7` as in step 2 over 10 rows.
- `ys` and `ye` `4400 + 24800*t`; `zs` and `ze` `28800 + 3000*sin(3.141592653589793*s) + 1200*sin(3.141592653589793*s)*(1 - cos(18.84955592153876*t))/2`. `xs` and `xe` are long formulas in s and t.
- All its calls, with the `xs` and `xe` formulas:

        get_guide {"part":"Two Towers > Prompt 11"}

### Curves, surfaces and material graphs by cards

Forms in the model, smooth and freeform, come from the commands `Freeform Curve`, `Loft`, `Sweep` and `Revolve`: part 9 (Forms, freeform curves and surfaces).

**Where a material's graph is stored.** The tools place, set and wire Material cards. One route through the door: `op:add material library=<set> name="X"` attaches a shipped texture set's ready-made graph. The 67 sets and their keys: part 7 (Materials).

Textures are photographs: the map cards bring a set's own images, and the nine sets marked `"grain": "luminance"` take their colour from `render_colour` (part 7).

Look it up: `albatross_place {"kind":"zz no such card"}` for the kinds; the ports of a card are in its own place answer; `albatross_graph {}` for what a graph holds; `get_guide {"part":"guide > 7. Materials"}` for materials.

## 11. UNION AI window: talking with the person
In this part: what the UNION AI window is, the two tools that serve it, how to speak to the person, and what your last message holds.

UNION AI is the chat window of UNION. Pictured: the title UNION AI, two tabs (CENTRAL, Agents), a LEADS column with a New lead button, an OUTPUTS column and a box Ask UNION AI. The File actions (New, Open, Save As, Close, Exit, Print, every Import and Export) are the person's presses too: UNION refuses them to you and names the control.

The window has a command. Press it to open the window, then take its picture:

    commands_run {"name":"gooseClicked"}
    view_image {"window":"falcon","width":1100}

With the window not open, `view_image {"window":"falcon"}` answers `cannot proceed: the falcon window is not open; its program tile's command opens it`. Press the command first.

**The two tools**

    falcon_wait {"timeout_ms":15000}
    falcon_say {"text":"<one short sentence>","done":true}

- `falcon_wait` takes the person's next prompt. Its reply is `falcon.wait` in the reference. `falcon_wait {"timeout_ms":1000}` with nothing waiting answered `{none:true}`.
- `falcon_say` shows `text` as your words. `done` true marks your final answer. Its reply is `falcon.say` in the reference.
- `falcon_say` answered: `cannot proceed: FALCON has not been opened in this window, so there is nowhere to show these words; ask the person to open FALCON`.

**How to talk**

- Decide and act. Where the person's words leave a choice that changes the result (type, place, count, level, view), choose it and say what you chose. The door's own words: ask only when the job cannot be done without the answer.
- Ask nothing that the model, the counts or a look-up answers.
- Each message to the person is one short sentence: what happened and, when the next press is theirs, that press. Example: "The walls are in; press Save."
- A refusal that names a control of theirs: do not retry; name the control to press.
- A busy answer such as "another AI chat's drawing call is still running in UNION; retry in a moment": wait, retry.

**What the last message holds**

- Counts read back from UNION with `document_info {"categories":true}`.
- What you chose where the words left a choice.
- Where UNION refused: its own words, quoted exactly, and the press that is the person's.
- Where a thing did not go through: what you sent and UNION's answer.

## 12. Large models: what to do about them
In this part: what drives the cost, and what to do about it.

**What costs**

- With the 3D view in front, every write rebuilds it.

**What to do**

- Edit with a plan view in front: `views_list {}`, then `view_activate` the plan by its id (a name two views share is refused). Show the 3D view once after a run of writes with `view_activate {"view":"{3D}"}`, then take several pictures with `view_camera` and `view_image`.
- Send 25 to 35 op lines per `ops_run` on a big model; the tool takes up to 500.

Look it up: `document_info {"categories":true}`; `views_list {}`; `get_guide {"part":"guide > 6. See your work"}` for part 6 (See your work).

## 13. UNION's words: answers to retry, answers that end the matter
Every answer of UNION is in words. A refusal names its fix and often lists the valid words. Read the words, not only the colour: a green step can carry a note.

In this part:
- Answers that mean wait and retry (a drawing call still running, busy, unavailable, still building), and the answers that look like a wait and are not.
- The refusal table. Rows 1 to 28 are step lines, ribbon keys and the options strip. Rows 29 on are the door's tools, ops and ALBATROSS. Row numbers are fixed: other parts quote them.
- A wrong word on purpose: UNION lists the valid words.

Answers that end the matter are rows 31, 32 and 35 (the File band, Undo of the person's change). Do not retry them; tell the person which control to press. For every other answer: read the words, fix the line, send it again.

Look it up:

    commands_list {"name":"<command name>"}
    views_list {}

Both list the valid words.

### Answers that mean wait and retry
Send the same call again after a moment, unchanged, unless the row says to ask the person first.

| UNION's words or state | what it means | next |
|---|---|---|
| "another AI chat's drawing call is still running in UNION; retry in a moment" | one drawing call runs at a time; another AI's call holds it. Not a failure | send the same call again; repeat while it answers so |
| "cannot proceed: the 3D view is still building its model; ask for the picture again in a moment" (`view_image`, no picture) | the 3D view in front has not stood whole after the wait of up to 20 seconds | ask again; if it answers so again, send the call under "Still building without end" |

### Still building without end
The answer "still building" can come while UNION is idle: the main window is minimised or hidden behind the UNION AI window. This call still returns the picture as it stands:

    view_image {"window":"main"}

Name no `view` in it.

Edit with a plan view in front, then show the 3D view once and take several pictures.

    views_list {}
    view_activate {"view":"<floor plan id>"}

Part 6 (See your work) holds the rest.

### Answers that look like a wait and are not
- "cannot proceed: the Albatross window did not open" (row 38): ask the person to open ALBATROSS, then send the call again.

### Refusal table for step lines, ribbon keys and the options strip
A red step changes nothing unless noted. Rows 1, 2 and 28 come from `start:` steps: on the person's door a `start:` step is red with the words of row 31.

| # | UNION's words | what it means | fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "start: no New picker in this build" | `start:New` is not a template | `start:Architectural` or another listed template |
| 2 | "no document is open: the ribbon is hidden on the Start page" | a ribbon step before `start:` | `start:<template>` first |
| 3 | "an unknown segment '—' -" | a line without all five parts | five parts, middle dot between, em dash for an empty part. The short step `qa:Undo · expect —` was also played green |
| 4 | "'9' stands after the kind; every other word is a key=value" | `name=Level 9` unquoted | `name="Level 9"` |
| 5 | "the step left the modal ... open: closed by the player (a window: "<title>", buttons ...; name the answer in the step's fields as `<title>: <button>=`)" | a dialog stood with no answer, or a table row was pressed with no OK | `fields <Dialog>: <field>=<value>` and `keys Return` (played green), or the button in fields |
| 6 | (no words) nothing placed after a Filled Region or Floor sketch | Escape instead of Finish | `contextual:Finish` |
| 7 | "cannot proceed: the sketch is not closed -- its open end is at (-600, -410) mm" | the loop did not close | repeat the first point exactly. The Region sketch stays open: `keys Escape Escape` |
| 8 | "unknown expect form 'tool stands'"; "status '' NOT read"; "unknown expect form 'dialog'" | a free-text expect | a count, `nothing selected`, `view … active`, `dialog closed` |
| 9 | `Sheets +1` (any sheet count) reads 0 -> 0 and the step goes red | sheets are not a counted kind | `dialog closed`; UNION's msg "Sheet A150 created" |
| 10 | "the key '195' is not a key this stage knows" | text typed as one word | one key per character |
| 11 | a step that starts `annotate:` or `text:` does not play | a guessed name | `ribbon:Annotate:Text` with keys |
| 12 | "no chrome control 'Ground' (30 words known here)" | a view tab is not a chrome word; the words name `Activate View` on a viewport | do the plan work before the sheet |
| 13 | "an Aligned dimension takes references, and no live element stands within this command's own tolerance of the click" | the pick was off any geometry (26 mm off) | pick endpoints of existing lines |
| 14 | "cannot proceed: nothing under the click to tag" (Keynote) | the pick was on empty space | pick on a real element |
| 15 | "the options strip has no 'Offset' (its options: Storey (Level), Width, Height, Diameter, Middle Elevation, Lock, Apply, Start Offset, End Offset, System Type)" | `Offset` or `Size` sent to a Duct; the words list the strip's options | Width, Height, Middle Elevation |
| 16 | "'System Type' has no item 'zzz' (its items: Supply Air / Return Air / Exhaust Air)" | a wrong choice item | one of the three |
| 17 | "table 'Patterns' has no row 'zzz' (its rows: Solid fill, Diagonal crosshatch, ...)"; the same for Styles, Weights, Arrowheads, Categories | a wrong row | this IS how to read a table's rows |
| 18 | "table 'Views' has no row 'Timber Eaves Detail' (its rows: Ceiling Plan, 3D View, Drafting View, Schedule, Schedule, Schedule)" | Place View lists kinds | name the row as listed: `Views=Drafting View` |
| 19 | "cannot proceed: view already on a sheet: A150" | a standing Viewport tool still holds the placed view, or a second placement | `keys Escape Escape`, then press Viewport again; a view sits on one sheet |
| 20 | "the Viewport tool standing was ended by Modify" | `plan:select` ends a standing tool | use it only after placement |
| 21 | "cannot proceed: Duct works in a plan, section or elevation view: a sheet is in front; use Activate View on one of its viewports to work in that view" | a sheet is the active view | ducts and terminals BEFORE the sheet |
| 22 | Ducts 0 -> 1 after three picks | the third pick starts a segment Escape throws away | two picks per duct |
| 23 | "cannot proceed: a level named Roof already exists" | the template names Ground, Level 1, Roof | another name |
| 24 | "cannot proceed: sheet number exists: A102" | template sheets A000, A100 to A103, A201 ... | a new number |
| 26 | "no contextual tab stands to press 'Cancel' on (waited 0 ms, nothing selected)" | no sketch stood: the step before ended it (a Detail Line press) | press Cancel while the sketch stands |
| 27 | "'Category' has no item 'Detail Items'" (Load Block) | the Category list in that dialog did not hold it | choose an item the list holds |
| 28 | "the active view is 'Level 1' (expected 'Ground')" | the Structural template opens on Level 1, not Ground | `expect view Level 1 active` after `start:Structural` |
